are those of the internal market, competition and budgetary discipline, while social rules remain vague, elusive and devoid of any mechanism for sanctions in the event of violation. i will leave it to mrs ghilardotti to speak on behalf of my group on the general framework, and i will concentrate on two other aspects: the revision of the 1994 directive on european works councils and merger and acquisition procedures. the definitions of information and consultation in the workers' councils directive are so vague that they offer no guarantees. the definition of consultation as 'exchanging views and establishing a dialogue' is far too vague. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the workers' representatives are consulted in the planning phase, that the works council can give an opinion, that it can propose alternative solutions and that negotiations can be started not only on the basis of the management plan but also on the basis of the counter-proposals of the workers' representatives. i believe that we must finally affirm the possibility of bringing a matter before a competent public authority at national level, as already provided for in the 1998 directive on collective redundancies, and, where appropriate, at european level, particularly in groups of community size, so that if the procedure for information and prior consultation has not been respected, or if the decisions are manifestly unfounded and other solutions could be considered in the social and employment fields, the competent public authority can declare the abolition plan null and void. the 1994 directive must therefore be revised - i share your analysis, commissioner - otherwise this text, which was pioneering at the time of its adoption, would end up being behind the times in the light of the new wording adopted by the council, as regards the european public limited company, or by parliament in 1999, at first reading, on the directive on a general framework. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will then be able to take a decision on the proposal. secondly, and finally, with regard to mergers. i do believe that the employment dimension must really be taken into account, and this is possible without a revision of the treaties, simply by a change in legislation, because the treaties already give the commission the task of ensuring that these decisions have an impact on employment. i therefore believe that not only is the proposed questionnaire indispensable, but that the workers' representatives must be able to bring the matter before the commission if they consider that the proposed merger threatens employment or the maintenance of industrial sites, and that not only the commissioner responsible for competition but also the commissioner responsible for employment and social affairs should be able, if necessary, to challenge the conditions provided if they do not sufficiently guarantee the maintenance of employment.

commission - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, today the commission adopted its proposals for the specific programmes of the framework programme for research 2002-2006. at the same time, it adopted a communication on the possible use of article 169 of the treaty for the implementation of the framework programme. the specific programmes are instruments for implementation. the commission's proposals on this subject therefore contain nothing more than the proposal for the framework programme, which must be adopted by codecision. but they do provide a number of clarifications on this subject. as you know, the commission adopted the framework programme on 21 february last, and this new framework programme is specifically designed to help achieve the european research area. i would remind you of the main principles. in this context, we have presented the framework programme with the intention, on the one hand, of concentrating efforts on a limited number of priorities where community action has the greatest added value. we are also looking to try to create a structuring effect on research in europe, through greater achievement between national activities with a view to creating a more coherent european research area. we also believe that the management of our framework programmes must be lightened and simplified by the methods of intervention used. for the implementation of this framework programme, we propose a structure of five specific programmes. it ultimately reflects that of the framework programme, whose political project it translates into operational reality. the structure is as follows: a programme entitled 'integrating and strengthening the european research area' which brings together all research activities and coordination of research policies in europe, a programme 'structuring the european research area' which includes activities in the field of the relations between research and innovation, in the field of the mobility of researchers and in the field of infrastructure and science and society issues, and its links with citizens, issues which are increasingly important in european society. we also have a programme for research activities in the field of euratom. the commission has also proposed two programmes for the activities of the joint research centre, one in the non-nuclear field and the other in the nuclear field. the content of the proposals is intended to provide details of the scientific and technological content presented in much greater detail than in the framework programme. but they also concern the new implementation instruments which are at the heart of the philosophy of the 2002-06 framework programme, the creation of networks of excellence and integrated projects. further details on the operation will be provided in the rules for participation and dissemination of the framework programme adopted in codecision, for which the commission will present its proposals at a later date. i also told you that for the communication on the implementation of article 169 of the treaty, which never actually came into force, we had a series of suggestions prepared on the practical way in which the formula of community participation in jointly implemented national programmes could work. that is the meaning of article 169. we therefore want to launch a political debate on this issue. on the basis of these initial results, the commission intends to submit a proposal for a framework decision setting out the general conditions for community support under article 169 and the possible areas of use of this formula. i think, madam president, that this is the first time that the commission has put forward its proposals for specific programmes shortly after it has presented the proposal for a framework programme. we believe that we are thus responding to a request from parliament to facilitate the political debate by providing this series of supplementary information. there are also elements of clarification and clarification, since the new instruments require it, and we have also planned an information session with the members of the committee on industry, foreign trade, research and energy on 5 june. i think we will have done our best to adopt, within the time-limits set, at parliament level and with the council, the new framework programme which is a tool for this european research area, which i believe is largely supported by the european union. - mr president, a real environmental policy must be pursued in europe, to respect the environment, our environment. it is the recognition of the duty to pass on to future generations an intact universal natural heritage. however, we must ensure that environmental policy in europe is not ideological but is based on the notion of responsibility. let us apply the principle of subsidiarity in the management of pollution problems. for example, urban air pollution must be dealt with by local authorities with maximum freedom of action. the pollution of a river's waters affects the river states. they are free to provide solutions, the main thing being that they are effective. on the other hand, global climate change is global. europe must have a common position in international forums on this subject and must give the member states, through framework directives, objectives to be achieved, leaving them full latitude to achieve them. in conclusion, let us not regulate everything from brussels or strasbourg. decisions taken closer to the citizen will be more appropriate and necessarily better understood. is this not the european union's ambition, to be better understood by the peoples?

and monitoring of developments. it has felt that time has been short, but i would still like to say that we have received more than a hundred written comments, and in good time. almost all environmental organisations, social organisations and even large business organisations have formulated their proposals and sent them to the commission. we also looked very carefully at the draft report by mr hulthén. in our proposal, we have said on behalf of the commission that we obviously want to make sure that this becomes a proposal that is owned jointly by many different stakeholders in society, and that we want to follow it up in such a way that we also consult different groups in society. in this context, parliament will of course also play an active role. it can be said that the commission's proposal for a sustainable development strategy has also remained the same during the examination of this proposal. the priorities we set at the outset have been there all along, and the proposals have been recognised along the way. i would also like to comment on what has been said about the international perspective. because it's incredibly important. we have said on behalf of the commission that we must come back to be even more concrete and follow up on our views on how we should act internationally. it is important that we sweep our own front door and show how we are going to deal with these issues and show leadership before we start telling the rest of the world how to do it. of course, the global perspective must be present in everything we do. at the same time, our sustainable development strategy also emphasises, as marit paulsen pointed out, that we must ensure that we get rid of what is an inconsistent policy and get rid of subsidies that are actually not good for the environment and that do not promote sustainable development. i think that is clearly stated in the programme. it now remains to be dealt with at the council meeting in gothenburg. it is an important task to ensure that it is not watered down at this meeting, but that we can actually stand on such an ambitious platform as the commission's strategy and get all the member states to work towards its implementation. i think it is a good objective for the belgian presidency to follow up the way we heard jonckheer describe it in the debate. i also think that it is important, as was also mentioned in the debate, that we look at how the european parliament and our own institutions should be changed in such a way that we too can live up to the idea of sustainable development and create these links between economic and social issues and environmental issues. we must also, in the european parliament, in the commission and in the council, probably review our way of working so that it can be effective and so that we have a way of tackling the issues that go beyond borders and not just look at narrowly defined areas. it will be exciting to look back at our policies in areas such as agriculture and fisheries, transport and compensation. it is, of course, up to us and the union as a whole to prove that. these were probably the most important comments, apart from the question raised by mr corbey, namely how implementation should be carried out. i would like to say that i have, at any rate, from the outset, made it very clear that we have good legislation, solid legislation, as was also shown in the evaluation of the fifth environmental action programme. at the same time, we must also ensure that this legislation is implemented. it is therefore important that we also ensure that we have a good control of implementation in this area. it is certainly possible to devise further measures to strengthen monitoring, but what we are already doing to ensure that member states are complying with the legislation will be strengthened. we must also make it clearer to our citizens in the union how the member states are behaving. i think it might help to put pressure on the countries. finally, i would just like to comment on how we define sustainable development, because it was raised in the blokland report. notice that in the commission's strategy for sustainable development we start by quoting the brundtland commission report and its definition of sustainable development. the paragraph that defines it also contains a line of reasoning on how to combat poverty. of course, it is extremely important. i stress again the importance of a global perspective, but if you read the brundtland commission report carefully, our definition is the correct one. i think it is important that we stick to this definition. it is a superiority and it points to our responsibility to future generations, which is what it is all about. thank you for this debate. let us see that we too can put this into practice. (applause) i would like to thank you.
the council. mr president, i would like to thank you for your reply. i would like to make a few comments on what has been said in the debate. several speakers have addressed the issue of economic growth and its impact on the environment. there is a little outdated idea that economic growth always leads to environmental degradation. however, we know, as has also been pointed out, that poor economic development entails great risks of environmental degradation. the english concept of decoupling, i.e. the importance of being able to separate the curves of economic development from those of environmental impact, is becoming increasingly central to the environmental policy debate. this is not really new. we've been working on it for many decades without perhaps using that very term. looking at the eu in a ten-year perspective, i would guess that growth in the eu has been about 30 percent. at the same time, greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by 4%. this means that for every million euros of production, greenhouse gas emissions are reduced by about 35%. it's an expression of the decoupling that's already happening. at the same time, we must be even more successful and ensure that it is not just a marginal reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. over the next few decades, a radical reduction will be required. the nox emissions in sweden per million euro produced are today about 60 per cent lower. the corresponding figure for sox emissions is about 80 percent. these are two more examples of decoupling. it is now time to step up our efforts even more, and to do so in those areas where we have not been able to detect a reduction in environmental impact today and where economic growth has been a contributing factor. the question of subsidies and internalisation of costs was also raised by several speakers. as i said in my opening speech, i regard it as a central issue in environmental policy thinking, now and for a long time to come. at the global level, it is truly astonishing that we have today subsidies, by some estimates, amounting to 200 billion dollars a year to non-sustainable energy, i.e. fossil fuels. it is an unimaginably large sum, which shows that instead of internalizing environmental costs, we have actually externalized environmental costs and carried them elsewhere. the main line of development in the eu, and indeed globally, must be to eliminate this type of subsidy and to focus instead on a real internalisation of environmental costs in prices. biodiversity has also been mentioned here, and it is a little bit of a heart issue for me. i would point out that we have major problems with biodiversity in europe too, something that very few people are really aware of. some 35 percent of all bird species are threatened, and as many as 45 percent of butterfly species, to take two examples. we are not achieving these objectives by simply establishing natura 2000 sites, although this is an important part of a nature conservation policy. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council at the next meeting of the european council. many of the endangered species depend on the small-scale agricultural landscape, which is now disappearing. it is really important to prevent this from happening in the new countries, which we hope will become members of the eu. however, it is not just a matter of integrating this thinking into agricultural policy, but it must also be done in fisheries policy. the state of marine biodiversity is much worse than that of land biodiversity. in fact, the marine ecosystems off our coasts are in a real crisis. if european citizens could see with their own eyes what we are really doing to the seabed and to seawater and the effects this has on biodiversity, it would probably be a revolution in environmental policy in the eu. it is therefore important to integrate environmental considerations into fisheries policy and to consider marine ecosystems as important components of the biodiversity we must work to preserve. it has also been pointed out by jonckheer that sectoral focus is at odds with environmental policy in the eu. this is precisely what we are going to remedy by sectoral integration. i also agree with mr schörling that this is going a little too slowly. i therefore hope that the gothenburg summit, on the basis of the presidency's synthesis report, will be able to provide clear and precise guidelines for the further work on sectoral integration. i think, mr president, that i am satisfied with these comments.

mr president, on the eve of the gothenburg summit, it was necessary to reconcile environment and economic growth, that is to say, to combat environmental degradation while giving businesses the means to develop. the sixth action programme is trying to do this with varying degrees of success. it suggests ratifying kyoto to combat the greenhouse effect effectively and insists on the need for greater protection of the cultural and natural heritage, as my colleague mr de veyrac has stressed in his report, on which we agree. but there are other things which worry us, namely that we are moving to the sixth programme without any real evaluation of the results of the previous programme, the fifth, which is totally abnormal. we feel that a ten-year programme is far too long, so much so that in the commission's communication, which is a 90-page document, theory takes precedence over practice. as regards transparency of decisions and access to documents, i hope that they will not be left as a dead letter, as the korhola report recommends. finally, the objectives of strengthening the protection of biodiversity through the natura 2000 network are of concern. almost all member states have implementing difficulties due to the vagueness of the texts and their restrictive interpretation by the european court of justice. article 225a of the treaty of nice provides for the possibility of creating judicial chambers responsible for hearing at first instance certain categories of actions in specific matters. it is very likely that the environment will be one of the first areas to be installed, given the context. is this the way to protect the environment? let me put this in doubt and call for a sixth programme which is rational, realistic and humanistic in its application.
commission. – mr president, members of the european parliament, thank you for your interventions and, of course, first of all i would like to commend the rapporteur, mrs myller, for her excellent work - doc. a5-0176/2001 by mr dell'alba, on behalf of the committee on budgets, on the proposal for a council regulation (ec, ecsc, euratom) on the financial regulation applicable to the general budget of the european communities (com (2000) 462 - c5-0627/2000 - 2000/0203 (cns)).
- thank you, mr van hulten. - thank you very much. i assure you, you have been translated perfectly into dutch.
the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have to say that i am very pleased with the way the commission has been working. on 26 july last year the commission proposed a fundamental revision of the financial bible, the financial regulation, with basic provisions for the whole of financial management. today we have the opportunity to debate the amendments and the reports of parliament. i would like to begin by expressing my gratitude and my admiration for two gentlemen, namely the rapporteur for the committee on budgets, mr dell'alba, and the rapporteur for the committee on budgetary control, mr van hulten. you have done a very comprehensive job in a very short time, and for that i express my admiration and my gratitude. i would also like to thank the committees for their intensive and precise work. we now have the reports of the rapporteurs, the report of the court of auditors, which was published in march, and the draft recommendation of the council. i would like to stress in particular how valuable it is that parliament supports this tight timetable, this ambitious timetable, namely to have a new budgetary regulation available as early as 2002 and, thanks to your work, we are very well on schedule. the whole procedure is not an easy situation, as has been mentioned. unanimity is required in the council and the formal procedure for parliament provides for a simple consultation. the commission understands that parliament wants to make this procedure so that parliament's amendments can be reflected in the final result. you are aware of the proposal which the commission has put forward for the intergovernmental conference in nice. the commission has not yet formally adopted a position on parliament's amendments, as there is no formal opinion from parliament, but i would like to express my positive opinion on a number of amendments this evening. the results of the consultation with the council, the european parliament and the court of auditors show a high degree of agreement in many areas. in other areas there is still a need for clarification and coordination on matters of principle or technical details. i would like to return to some basic principles. the present financial regulation - it has been mentioned - dates from 1977 and we have at the moment more of a patchwork of financial and budgetary rules than a coherent approach. the proposal therefore involves a fundamental simplification and restructuring. the aim is to consolidate all the principles and essential rules governing financial management in a single legal instrument. i am therefore also reluctant to accept various amendments which propose to insert specific elements. detailed and technical provisions should be laid down in the implementing regulation to be adopted by the commission. the commission proposal is divided into two parts, as i have already said: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the first part sets out more rational rules for almost all the areas covered by the current financial regulation. the principles of annuality and unity should be more strictly applied. the commission is very pleased that parliament supports this position and this recasting. this will simplify the procedure for carrying over appropriations to the next financial year. the second important point is that we must eliminate negative expenditure and negative revenue. negative expenditure in the agricultural sector is to be treated as earmarked revenue in accordance with the rules applicable to this sector. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the interinstitutional agreement provides - and even includes - that expenditure financed by assigned revenue is not to be included in the ceiling of the financial perspective. that is one of the main reasons why we say that this agricultural revenue should be earmarked for specific purposes. if it is not, then agricultural expenditure must be cut back from today's level, and that should be avoided. the budgetary procedure should not be used to impose a kind of free-for-all cap on agricultural expenditure. one of the important objectives of the revision is to ensure that commitments for external aid are translated more rapidly into concrete projects. in the interests of more rigorous implementation, it is therefore proposed that global commitments be disbursed by 31 december of financial year n+1, except for the implementation of financial conventions in the context of external policies. the new version transposes the eu directives on public procurement into the financial regulation. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the award of contracts for the supply of services by the railway undertakings. as regards financial assistance, fundamental principles such as the existence of a legal basis are clearly stated. the proposal also provides for the decentralisation of all external aid to third countries. this is another aspect which has been mentioned frequently by the committee on budgets in the sense of increasing efficiency. the second part proposes a sound system of financial management oriented towards results and performance. this system has two key components, namely the increased responsibility of the managers and the integration of controls into the management of funds. i can only support what mr van hulten has said. it's about making accountability. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary authority is able to meet its obligations. the responsibility should be shared by all those who have to deal with resources. it is then impossible to carry out this very concealment. that is a key point. mrs theato, you have just said in your amendments - which the commission of course does not welcome because they would undo the whole system - that the latest fraud report would now prove the importance of ex ante controls. i have to say this simply because the statistics in this report are the statistics of the financial controllers in the member states. that is to say, it is the statistics which are reported, for example in the customs field. in the customs field there is no ex ante control at all. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the payments are not controlled by the centralized ex ante control here in brussels, but by the paying agencies in the member states. this is the case with structural funding. the question of whether or not we want to have ex ante controls further centralised and the statistics from the member states are simply not related, because ex ante controls are not located there but in the member states. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we are proposing, in the spirit of activity-based budgeting, to abolish the separation between a and b. this is not to reduce transparency, of course, but to increase it. it will not be the case in future that the human resources or the administrative resources will no longer be shown separately. of course they will continue to have their own extra budget, which will then be decided by parliament together with the council. but it is no longer a global part that is summarized in the budget, but it is allocated to the individual policy areas. and that, in general, increases transparency. the following points are consistent with the commission's position. i now refer to the amendments by the rapporteurs on the role of the players, the primacy of the budgetary regulation over sectoral rules or provisions, the definition of commitment, externalisation. i would also like to welcome amendment no 44 on the definition of a financial statement and its function. i think that is a very important clarification, as indeed individual clarifications are contained in the amendments, which are very much welcomed by the commission because i think they substantially increase the manageability and legal clarity which the financial regulation is intended to create. i have already mentioned that we cannot accept the amendments on negative revenue and expenditure. let me say this about that. as regards customs revenue, your amendments propose that the proportion of administrative appropriations which can be retained in the member states should be entered in the budget as expenditure. it would be a category 5 expenditure and would create entirely new problems in that category, even though it is money that does not flow through the commission's budget at all. i think that we can still come together on these points. i think it is not useful to comment on all the various amendments now, because that would go far beyond midnight. let me conclude by saying that the european parliament does want to postpone the formal vote on the resolution for the time being. i would like to reiterate that i understand and support the european parliament's wish to give weight to its position in the negotiations. i therefore intend to ask the presidency to hold a quadrilateral meeting with the european parliament, the court of auditors and the commission at the ecofin council next week, on 5 june, in order to be able to vote on the further procedures in a quadrilateral meeting, but above all to be able to speak on the substance. this meeting should then take place as soon as possible. i hope that this procedure will enable the european parliament to adopt its formal opinion in good time. the commission would like to present its revised proposal in september in the light of further developments and hopefully further agreement.

is it not rather the role of our states to enforce the law, and to check that there is no breach of the law? so what are the possibilities? we must get out of this dialectic which promised women's liberation and only proposed a competition with our male partners to become superwomen. we are not a clone of man, we are not a cog in the production system. women's rights cannot be separated from the recognition of their specificity. our society is longing for a new feminism. we are women, wives and mothers. as women, we want to evolve according to our own model, our own sensibility, our own intuition and our own intelligence. man can never be the sole reference point for the development of the human being. as spouses, complementarity between men and women implies necessary cooperation in professional, social and family life. as mothers, we carry the future of humanity and, mrs hautala, you are right to stress that nothing should prevent a woman from giving birth. so yes to gender equality, but with respect for the specificity and dignity of each individual.

- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the very useful report by mr ribeiro y castro mentions in particular the need for transparency and the importance of reliable employment statistics. it is true that in my country, france, the government can announce a supposedly dramatic fall in unemployment when in reality it is stagnating or even increasing. since the beginning of the year, plans for redundancies have followed plans for redundancies: marks and spencer is relocating, danone is rationalising others, and red flags have been fired at companies that are laying off workers while making a profit. but governments bear their share of the responsibility, for the original european project of free movement and competition between countries with comparable living standards and social protection has been replaced by the indiscriminate opening up of capital and products manufactured elsewhere in europe under conditions akin to slavery. for companies subject to laws imposed by parliaments and states, the labour market is not just european, it is global. for workers it is a different matter, and i note that, very rightly, recital c of mr ribeiro y castro's report states that 'a high degree of geographical mobility in the labour market is not an end in itself'. two hundred thousand french people, overwhelmed by the burden of taxes and the endless burdens of administration in their own country, did not wait for eures to finally go to work and live better, at least they hope, in the united kingdom. so having a network to enable those who want to find a job in another eu country is certainly a useful thing. but enabling companies to create jobs for nationals in their own country must remain our priority.

in writing. - the nice european council, held from 8 to 11 december 2000, allowed the intergovernmental conference to make some progress. in particular, the following were mentioned: declaration 23 on the future of the union, and the launching of a 'broad and in-depth debate'; - the revision of article 7 of the eu treaty on respect for fundamental rights in the member states; - the increase in the powers of the president of the commission and his appointment by the qualified majority of the council, which, combined with the recent proposals of the french prime minister, lionel jospin, on the latter's election, make it possible to considerably strengthen his legitimacy and therefore his authority. this resolution should encourage the heads of state or government to go further, in particular by calling for a convention to be convened in the image of the one which was responsible for drawing up the charter of fundamental rights, and whose participation is indispensable in the next revision of the treaties. this convention cannot be content with being a mere forum: we want it to participate actively and normatively in the debate and drafting of the next treaty in a constitutional form. it is essential that the national parliaments ratify the treaty of nice: the theory of a crisis of refoundation which would justify an appeal for non-ratification is a chimera, which puts enlargement at risk and prohibits the necessary debate which is about to begin.
in writing. - yesterday we saw in this house a good example of one of the methods usually used in european affairs to conceal problems and to prevent them from being raised in public opinion. in the debate on the treaty of nice, there was little talk of anything other than the 'after-nice'. all the federalist speakers took the floor one after the other to call for the establishment, at the next laeken council, under the belgian presidency (which was a presidency favourable to ultra-federalism), of a "convention" which would open a "constituent process" which should produce a "european federal constitution" which the 2004 intergovernmental conference would be asked to adopt. the ratification of nice is therefore taken for granted. it's not even a question. the debate on 2004 is driving the debate on nice, before the debate on 2010 is undoubtedly used to obscure the debate on the future draft submitted for ratification in 2004. the immediate result is that virtually no one has spoken about nice, and public opinion is still as ignorant - except in ireland where a referendum is being held - of the content of a very important treaty which is to be submitted secretly for ratification by their national parliaments. we published our counter-report on the treaty of nice in an attempt to make the french debate escape this cover-up. in particular, it is essential to stress that the treaty of nice, as a whole, is fundamentally opposed to the spirit and the letter of the french constitution, which is the spirit of national sovereignty. some provisions are even openly contrary to it. these include: the introduction of an integration objective for the union and the community (article 43 teu), the standardisation of the status of members of the european parliament (article 190-5 tec), the creation of a status for political parties at european level (article 191 tec), the designation of the commission by qualified majority (article 214-2 tec), the approval by qualified majority of certain international cfsp agreements (article 24 teu), the new measures taken by majority for the introduction of the euro (articles 111 and 123-4 tec), the communitisation of international trade negotiations on services and intellectual property (article 133 tec), the inclusion of a community competence on 'modernising social security' (article 137 tec), or the introduction of military force, in the event of a rapid reaction, in the form of a military force (article 17 teu). it is extraordinary, in these circumstances, that the french government is not even considering bringing the matter before the constitutional council.
in writing. - everyone agrees that the disappointing results of the previous igc are symptomatic of the limitations of the purely intergovernmental method. the heads of state or government have acknowledged this in the declaration on the future of the eu annexed to the treaty. this has led the committee on constitutional affairs to demand that the convening of the new igc (responsible for the next revision of the treaties) be based on a radically different, transparent and open process. it proposes to draw inspiration from the effective and unanimously applauded method which led to the drawing up of the european charter of fundamental rights. it would therefore be necessary to convene a convention composed of members of the european parliament, national parliaments, the commission and the governments of the member states. it would meet at the beginning of 2002 and would be responsible for presenting to the igc (to be convened in the second half of 2003) a "constitutional proposal" based on the results of a wide public debate. this constitutional process will have to be translated into the adoption of an eu constitution. the report also calls on national parliaments to commit themselves to the convening of such a convention when they are called upon to vote on the treaty of nice. the treaty of nice, while generating a great deal of dissatisfaction, nevertheless removed the last formal obstacle to enlargement. that said, the accession of new member states requires a thorough review of the functioning of our institutions, which are often already on the verge of paralysis when we are only 15 member states. the debate is open. several political figures had the opportunity to contribute to the debate. the broadest possible range of actors and all european citizens must be involved. i would like to conclude by stressing that the charter of fundamental rights should be incorporated into the treaty in order to become binding. this would be a strong political signal to our fellow citizens. we now have three years to finally build institutions that ensure 'democracy', transparency and citizenship in the service of a strong european social project.
in writing. - the results of the intergovernmental conference in nice are in line with the expectations of the peoples of europe. first, the priority should have been the content of the union, with the needs and rights of each citizen being the first priority. we should have debated a real charter of social rights and freedoms, not ratified a cheap charter of fundamental rights. once the question of content had been raised, the question of fair financing of european policies should have been addressed, including a review of taxation and the requirement for democratic management mechanisms to meet these needs. taxing capital (a tobin tax) and punishing firms that lay off employees and make profits would have been a first step. the next question is the definition of container. europe must give itself the means of real democracy, dealing with all the major issues of society, respecting the diversity of the peoples of europe, while allowing the emergence of european citizenship. we must give workers and citizens the means to debate and influence labour law and economic choices, and control the executives and the central bank. the treaty of nice and the guidelines proposed in this report are the opposite of this approach. that is why i did not vote in favour.
in writing. - my colleagues in the french delegation from the union for a europe of nations group and i voted against the treaty of nice; but given the disparate nature of the motives of those who have also expressed themselves in this way, it seems necessary for us to specify our own in order to make things clear. we did not vote against the treaty of nice because it did not go far enough, as the most unbridled federalists think, or because it went too far, as a number of schizophrenics in the corridors who secretly dream of going back on their feet complain, but simply because it went in the wrong direction. however, we are very concerned about the suggestions made by this parliament, which are always at the forefront of the debate, when it comes to considering further surrenders of sovereignty by the nation states of the union, and we were pleasantly surprised by the final text: on the one hand, because, on the functional level, it represents a serious brake on the supranational drift which seeks to lead us as quickly as possible to the final disappearance of the states in favour of a bulimic and uncontrollable commission; the european parliament has been very active in the debate on the future of the union, and it has been very active in the debate on the future of the union. but despite these few healthy reactions, the treaty of nice has not been able to extricate itself from the logic that is deadly for european democracies and peoples, namely that of committing the european union, in accordance with declaration 23 on the post-nice process, to a 'constitutional' type of dynamic which can only lead to a european federal state whose assertion and future functioning are completely incompatible, despite the displeasure of the two heads of the french executive, mr chirac and mr jospin, with the persistence of nation states. and even if political semantics has already known some equally incongruous approximations as this impossible federation of nation states - let us remember the priceless democratic centralism - history teaches us that the peoples, sooner or later, no longer allow themselves to be fooled by what is, at best, a tragic mistake, at worst, an unforgivable lie. in writing. - as always, the construction of europe proceeds through successive trials and necessities. the essential test it has imposed on itself for the next few years, which is also a historical imperative, is naturally the choice to reconcile the geography of the continent with its history, and to proceed with the enlargement now made possible by the democratization and the considerable economic reforms of the ceecs. the treaty of nice, which the méndez de vigo report addresses and comments on with great honesty and rigor, is first of all the considerable political choice of a europe finally reunited under its founding values of democracy, freedom, solidarity and culture. the treaty of nice, it is true, did not provide the institutional reforms needed to achieve this considerable political ambition for our future, which alone justifies its ratification, but it did provide a democratic and coherent exercise of european political power by 27 countries and more. the difficulty of reaching agreement on the future institutions of the union, as stated in the treaty of nice, demonstrates the limits of intergovernmental action in an even larger number of member states. that is why i welcome the fact that our rapporteur proposes the creation of a convention, on the model of the one which drew up the european charter of fundamental rights, in order to prefigure and propose to the future igc a constitution for the future europe. we must not hide the fact that this will be a historic moment in the construction of europe, which is intended to bind our peoples and their future together irreversibly. that is why a democratic and public debate, an open debate between each of our peoples, must precede this pre-constitutional stage in order to remove any ambiguity about the europe we want to build together: a political europe or a business europe? a europe of power or a club of countries paralysed by the rule of consensus? the public debate decided at nice, like the method of the convention, which we have just affirmed here, are the conditions for this imperative democratization of debate and of the european issues.
in writing. - the anger of the federalists against the treaty of nice, which scrupulously echoes the méndez de vigo-seguro report, is surprising at first sight. far from being a change of course, far from initiating a fundamental reform of the process of european construction which would promote a harmonious reunification of our continent, the treaty of nice uses enlargement as a new justification and incentive to establish more supranationality, more centralisation, more super-states. the treaty of nice thus fits perfectly into the ideological line of its predecessors. it strengthens supranational institutions and creates new elements of supranationality such as european political parties or the unified statute for members of the european parliament. it incorporates the objective of integration into the treaties for the first time, applying it not only to the community but also, ideologically speaking, to the intergovernmental sphere. so why are there so many voices in the old pot of federalism, the european parliament, against a treaty which boldly deploys its dominant philosophy? could it be that we are, with nice, as georges berthu suggests, faced with the expression of a new avatar of federalism which is departing even more radically from the state component in favour of the one of numbers, the one of the importance of populations? the new weighting of votes in the council and the commission, closely linked to population levels, and the concept of a demographic net would then give a new face to the european institutions, where the notions of balance and parity would disappear in favour of the dominance of the states or groups of states with the largest population. this would lead to a europe no longer made up of equal (and equally respected) states but of unequal peoples. to put an end to this truly terrible drift, appealing to the old federalism against the new federalism is certainly not the right way. to avoid the undemocratic drift that threatens it, the european construction must be based on respect for national democracies. in writing. - the report we voted on today at first reading concerns a legislative proposal to improve directive 91/671/eec. this text, it must be admitted, has contributed to road safety in the european union. it has imposed the wearing of seat belts and the use of child restraints. these are essential in order to reduce the severity of injuries in the event of an accident. research on accidents has shown that children who are not restrained by a suitable device are seven times more likely to be seriously injured than those who are not. the revision of this text, which is ten years old, seems necessary. thus, under current legislation, children under 3 years of age may use a normal rear seat belt. as a father of young children, i am in a position to denounce this fact that endangers their health and lives. the restraints available on the market are now sufficiently advanced to be mandatory! the use of child restraints therefore needs to be further harmonised and made safer. the commission proposal also extends the scope of the directive to include the wearing of seat belts by the driver and seated passengers in all motor vehicles equipped with them. this proposal, while satisfactory, is not sufficiently precise. the committee on transport therefore wanted to make further clarifications. the commission is also proposing to launch an information campaign on the dangers of airbags for children carried forward in suitable seats with their backs to the road. as regards the safety of children under 12, i agree with the rapporteur that it is more logical to take their height into account rather than their weight, since they do not require any special equipment if they are at least 150 cm tall. it is our collective responsibility to ensure the safety of our children, and i voted for all the amendments that go along with it!

in writing. - for more than 30 years, the finances of the european communities and the union have been governed by an unchanged financial regulation, except for the implementing measures, and some 17 years will have passed before the draft reform of this regulation is adopted. the proposal for reform of the regulation on the union's budget which the european commission is submitting to the council of ministers is certainly one of the major texts of this parliamentary term, a text which will govern europe's finances for a long time to come. this is the importance of the renewed text which we are now submitting to parliament for the future of the european union. six vital areas are covered by this unprecedented reform proposal: reaffirmation of the principles of budgetary law, budget implementation, contracts and subsidies, accounting and reporting, the european union's external actions, as well as other major aspects such as discharge, the eaggf guarantee section, the structural funds, research and development, olaf and administrative appropriations. on 16 may, when adopting the draft report by mr dell'alba, the committee on budgets rightly pointed out that the primacy of the financial regulation over any other financial regulation should be specified in its own rules. it also asked, which seems to us to be the right thing to do, that the budget lines to which the revenue is allocated be more clearly specified, as well as the purpose of the appropriations. it also called for the inclusion in the community budget of all european agencies, including future agencies; however, to include these agencies in the annual vote of the budgetary authority would have the effect of making them lose all autonomy, when they were precisely created to be autonomous, with the european parliament voting on their annual grant and discharge. as regards the agencies, it is worth recalling that, apart from the fact that they must remain independent, olaf is dependent on the commission, whereas europol and eurojust are financed from national budgets. in writing. - the three reports on environment and development, which will be voted on in plenary on 31 may 2001, will set the tone for the preparations of the european parliament for the gothenburg summit of the fifteen. ten years after the concept of sustainable development was recognised as the development system that can reconcile economy and ecology, despite an armada of standards and regulations, globally, the environment has suffered more from development than it has benefited from it. while the concept of sustainable development seems to be understood by the commission and some member states, it is not generally understood by the fifteen. some members of the commission even continue to think of economic development in terms of duration, adjusting it to an environmental tip. yet the european union is draping itself in terms of sustainable development, while its agricultural, economic, transport, energy, foreign and development policies are stubbornly proving the opposite. the environmental aspect is always the last wheel of the cart. this is perfectly clear in the reports presented to the ep. the resolutions have been able to incorporate in concrete terms our responsibilities and obligations in the face of the continuing degradation of the planet, its warming and the disappearance of biodiversity, and they recall that only a reorientation of policies could attempt to reverse these trends. in this sense, the abolition of subsidies with a negative impact on the environment, eco-taxes, environmental responsibility, the subordination of the wto reform to the environmental component, the annual assessment of policy progress and the use of credible criteria are in the right direction. will the council and the commission have the courage to take up the ep's position? i doubt that. despite the great clarity of policy in dealing with the challenges of global warming and the oral and written commitments in treaties, directives and other international agreements, the actual achievement of these wishes remains very modest - for the record, it would require an 80 to 90% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions over 50 years to halt the warming process. 8% were granted. the fifteen are aware of these issues. will they have the heart and courage to change course and bracket and dare to tackle the reorientation of the cap, polluting transport and energy? otherwise, they will be faced with the economic, social, environmental and financial consequences of their political inconsistency.
