the rapporteur. - mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, after erika i, which initially tried to prevent environmental disasters by means of oil spills, erika ii, which complements it, also wants to be an instrument capable of properly assessing the consequences of such disasters and, in particular in the report which has been entrusted to me, of implementing better compensation for the victims concerned. we can only support this objective and we consider it essential to give it priority in view of the situation as it has developed, particularly in the wake of the erika disaster. at present there is an international system of liability and compensation for damage caused by oil pollution from ships, as established by the 1969 clc convention and the 1971 fipol convention, both of which were amended by the 1992 protocols. these two conventions established a two-tier system of liability based on objective but unfortunately very limited liability of the ship owner and on a compensation fund fund funded by the entities receiving the oil. among many countries in the world, all the coastal member states of the european union are now parties to both protocols, with the exception of portugal, which has not yet completed the ratification procedures. the united states, which has its own compensation scheme, the oil pollution act of 1990, is not a party to the agreement. the main problem with these two funds is that they are capped at eur 200 million. but in addition to the insufficiency of this amount, which is far exceeded in the case of the erika with an estimate of more than 300 million euros, this insufficiency causes a certain slowness in the procedure. fipol can only distribute what it has and must therefore wait for the exhaustive list of applications to know at what maximum rate it can compensate victims. for example, the forecasts for erika suggest that only two thirds of the sums committed by the victims will be covered, and this in a much too long period of time, even if provisional payments are made. the first initiative to remedy this situation is therefore to refer the matter to the imo, as the council has done, to reform the clc and fipol conventions in order to address several structural malfunctions. first, the ceiling should be raised: a first increase of eur 300 million is planned for 2003. the second is to extend the responsibilities to all the actors in the transport chain and, finally, to extend the conventions to include harmful and dangerous substances. we are of course in favour of this approach, but in the absence of reforms which would be difficult to achieve, europe had to intervene by means of a personal and adequate proposal. the commission has therefore proposed the creation of a community fund, called the cope fund, complementary to the fipol, modelled on its functioning, but with a ceiling of eur 1 billion. the fund would only be involved in the event of a maritime accident and would be fed by oil companies in member states receiving more than 150 000 tonnes of oil a year. it would be managed by the commission, which would be assisted by a committee composed of representatives of the member states. ladies and gentlemen, at this stage of my presentation, let me give you a brief outline of the consequences of tomorrow's vote. we believe, since the vote in the committee on transport, that an extension to all dangerous substances, an extension supported by the right and the left in parliament, however laudable it may be, will inevitably lead to a real blockage of the system. the conventions which are the basis for this enlargement have not yet been ratified. so does the european parliament really want this fund? i would like to remind you that we are determined to see that the victims of these major disasters, which have so far been caused almost exclusively by oil spills, are compensated in the most comprehensive and speedy way possible. how, then, can a third level of compensation be implemented, the cope fund, whose operation and procedures are modelled on the existing international system, by referring to conventions not yet recognized by the latter? by voting for the amendments of the committee on transport, there is a great risk, too great, it seems to me, of putting off any rapid implementation of the cope fund to the greek calendar. in addition to our amendments concerning the representativeness of local elected representatives in the compensation decision-making process, our separate vote requests are therefore aimed at restoring to some extent the subject of the original proposal and thus allowing the creation of a supplementary compensation fund at community level. this is a real emergency. how can we not be in favour of, on the one hand, taking care of all pollution ... (the president invites the speaker to conclude)... and, on the other hand, financial accountability for all those involved? we have to take responsibility. should we be theoretical environmentalists or should we set up as soon as possible ... (the president withdrew the floor)
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. - mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, these three reports actually reinforce the measures adopted by parliament last may in the context of the 'erika i package'. as regards the first report, which is that of mr sterckx, the european commission's proposal has two dimensions. firstly, we are working to improve the safety of ships, which is the basis of maritime safety. i am glad that the committee responsible has followed my proposal for a tighter timetable for the installation of black boxes and transponders on board ships. this means that all european vessels will have to be equipped with these devices by 2006 at the latest. secondly, we are proposing to the member states a community system of monitoring, control and information on traffic, which i am a little wary of, however, because there is not much of a community dimension to these measures. the european parliament has tried to consolidate its proposals, but they are still based on the efforts of the member states. the commission will be proposing a number of amendments to the proposal, including a number of amendments to the proposal for a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. parliament has been wise in asking for an assessment, after one year, of the measures to be taken to ensure that this proposal is actually implemented swiftly. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not affected by the crisis. that is why i am opposed to the notion of safe havens, which do not offer the same guarantees as ports in terms of naval equipment. the strengthening of communication between ports on the movements of ships carrying dangerous goods is another positive and important point. with this report, the european union is equipping itself with the instruments necessary for good cooperation between the member states and giving the member states more means of action to control and secure maritime traffic. we are thus protecting europe's marine and coastal environment, but we are also giving more rights to the captains and crews of the ship, including the most important right to avoid accidents at sea and thus protect themselves. the report by mr esclopé will enable us to give a new dimension to the cope fund project. the extension of the fund's scope of action to include pollution caused by harmful and dangerous substances is essential. we must ensure that this does not delay the first process. we must no longer be satisfied with a fund for compensation for damage caused by oil pollution, as the sinking of the ivoli sun off the coast of brittany has tragically shown. the proposal to make the owner of a ship responsible for marine pollution contribute to the compensation of victims seems to me to be a good one because it goes in the direction of making all the actors involved in maritime transport responsible. this concept of responsibility was not sufficiently defined in our legislation. the polluter pays principle is applied here, and it is applied fairly. it is a significant and positive change that may put an end to practices that are dangerous and harmful to our environment. finally, we shall vote on the report by our colleague, mr mastorakis, on the creation of a european maritime safety agency. the commission seems to be wary of his proposal. it has therefore introduced several paragraphs by which it intends to secure a veto on the functioning and work of this future agency. this clearly deprives the future agency of the independence which would be necessary for its effectiveness and credibility. i do not understand why the commission has wanted to put this agency under its control. parliament has therefore worked to reduce this dependence on the commission in order to give the agency enough power to justify its creation. the agency should only exist if it is independent and has real responsibilities. i believe that our work will give the agency greater responsibility and more autonomy to carry it out. there are two points in this proposal which do not satisfy me. firstly, the same report cannot call for unannounced inspection visits to the member states and at the same time require that these visits be carried out after consultation with the member state concerned. but if we have in mind two different types of visit, this is not clear in the text and it would be desirable to clarify it. secondly, i do not understand why our assembly has no representatives on the agency's board of directors, even though the commission appoints four from its own ranks and four from the professional organisations concerned and the council appoints four others. if we want to deprive parliament of representatives on this board in the name of the separation of powers, then we must also exclude the representatives of the council. the council is the community's co-legislator and the other branch of the budgetary authority alongside the parliament. if he is represented on the board of directors, then there is no real separation of powers and the absence of parliament's representatives makes no sense in these circumstances. these reservations aside, on the substance, the proposal for the creation of this agency, as amended by this house, i hope, seems satisfactory. we have done a lot to ensure that the european union has a single airspace. today we have taken a significant step towards a single maritime area in europe and i can only hope that we will continue to work towards this, particularly at international level, and that we will soon be able to draw the first lessons from the measures we have adopted.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, eighteen months ago the oil tanker erika broke in two off the coast of brittany, causing one of the greatest oil spills in history. unfortunately, this was not the first, and probably not the last, time that the coastline of one of our member states was so polluted. the french minister for the environment, for his part, had felt it unnecessary to shorten his holiday in réunion. did she underestimate the magnitude of the disaster? or did she think she was useless? it is true that mrs voynet and her green colleagues have other concerns than ecology, the number of seats the socialists will give them in the next parliamentary elections, the legalization of drugs, gay marriage, abortion, the legalization of immigrants who have entered france clandestinely, the protection of the lives of murderers in the united states - all subjects which leave little room for the environment. but our other leaders were very agitated. mr. jospin even went to one of the beaches, carried by his comrades who wanted to save him from dirtying his shoes. they all swore, but a little later, that they would never be allowed to go back. all arrangements would be made, double hulls, scrapping of floating wrecks, etc. some even came up with the idea of launching a boycott campaign against total, now france's only oil company. the major american oil companies rightly welcomed this welcome initiative. a year and a half later, this turmoil has brought little improvement. compensation for the victims is almost nil. only 6% of the available amount was paid. fipol, the compensation fund set up by the oil companies, seems to have as its main mission the payment of as little money as possible to the victims. the commission's procedures, its counter-investigations and its expert opinions seem to be designed to discourage the most persistent of the applicants, who are retreating in the face of the avalanche of measures imposed on them. our coastlines continue to be polluted by thousands of garbage ships. the 1996 conventions on compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea and the 2001 bunker convention on civil liability for damage in connection with pollution from oil-bunker bunkers are neither implemented nor ratified. what solutions do the three reports before us today offer? what about the victims' compensation? in his report, our colleague mr esclopé rightly notes that fipol is not very effective. but the question is whether the solution lies in the creation of a new compensation body. the maritime security of our countries ? the proposals in mr sterckx's report on the identification of ships, their loading and access to port are well justified, but they only deal with one aspect of the problem. as for the creation of a european maritime safety agency, as called for in the third report, mr mastorakis is right to question the usefulness of creating - and i quote the report - 'a new community bureaucracy'. once again, the europe of brussels seems to be restricting the freedoms of the member states by means of a new administration. but freedom is not license, and we should be perfectly clear about this. the flag assignment to a ship is a natural prerogative of the state, as the court of justice in the hague has recognized since the famous cases of the so-called mascate boots and the lotus ship. so we cannot object to the fact that liberia or panama, for example, use this attribute of their sovereignty. but this cannot lead to an obligation on our states to allow old ships with unskilled crews and serious environmental hazards to approach their coasts. a right of access and, where appropriate, of denial of access or diversion must be exercised in respect of any vessel entering the area defined by the montego bay convention as the exclusive economic zone, i.e. the 200 nautical mile zone. all these measures, even the wisest, fall short of the threats to our nations' coasts - ecological threats, of course - and perhaps some embarrassing questions should be asked to answer them. why, for example, is a french company obliged to use a foreign shipowner, whose flag is dubious and whose crew is a floating babel? the communist trade union cgt, which ruined the french shipyards, the governments which have increased the rate of compulsory levies by 15 points in 25 years probably have the answer. why is the oil we import not transported mainly by pipeline, much safer than any tanker? but the threats are not only ecological. the arrival of a turkish ship carrying a thousand kurds from syria, falsely presented as iraqi refugees, on the french riviera last february has shown the french that in the europe of schengen and amsterdam their maritime borders are no more controlled than their land borders, and this in the immediate vicinity of a major war port. any vessel can enter our territorial waters. today, some of these ships carry oil, others dangerous substances, still others illegal immigrants. tomorrow they might as well contain weapons or terrorist groups. these dangers are the result of the abolition of frontiers and the decline of our national navies, which today no longer have the means to fulfil their missions, chief among which is coastal protection. the restoration of maritime security in our countries, as in many other areas, does not require new european regulations so much as governments whose policy is based on simple principles: energy independence, maintenance of a genuine national navy, reduction of the burden and protection of frontiers, including maritime frontiers.

- mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, although a number of questions remain, i would like to say at the outset that i agree with the three reports which have been presented to us for the erika ii package, stressing the urgency of their adoption and a fortiori for the future with regard to implementation. improvements are still needed and, i hope, possible; that is the point of the rapporteur. mr president, my report also deals with the implementation of article 299 (2) of the treaty of amsterdam, which concerns the outermost regions, in the fisheries sector. this treaty recognized the specific nature of these regions and defined them both by their handicaps and their difficulties, linked to their remoteness, insularity, often hostile terrain and climate, and sometimes even economic dependence. once signed, it made it possible to adapt the policies concerned legitimately, without, however, calling into question the coherence of the community legal order. in the fisheries sector, seven regions and three states are concerned. for the member states, spain, portugal and france. for the regions, the azores, madeira, the canary islands, guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion. various derogating measures are therefore allowed for both fisheries and regional policy, that is to say our structural funds. the report i am presenting approves of course this adjustment, but at the same time a number of amendments have been tabled, on which i should like to speak briefly. i am putting down one, in particular, which was adopted by the committee on fisheries. this is amendment no 5 which concerns, and this is very important for those concerned, the fishing vessels, the financial intervention rates of the fifg, the financial instrument, in these outermost regions. the commission proposes that the community's participation rate in these regions should be increased, which is a good thing, up to a maximum of 85%, except for fleet renewal and modernisation of fishing vessels and pilot projects which keep the same participation rates as in the previous regulation and are therefore not changed. my amendment and the amendment of the committee on fisheries therefore deal with this 'except'. the commission proposes that, in the case of modernisation and renewal of the fleet, the community's intervention rate should not be increased and the private self-financing rate should not be reduced for this renewal and modernisation. we do not think that this is the right approach and does not serve the treaty objectives of economic recovery for these regions. it is therefore appropriate, and this is what is proposed to you, to change these rates in group 2. this would have a positive impact on the development of coastal fisheries, as well as on the improvement of the treatment of catches, and would meet the expectations of the players in this sector. on the other hand, if there is overcapacity in the metropolitan area, it is not the case, or in any case, it is much less safe, in all the outermost regions. finally, parliament has emphasized the need to improve safety on board vessels, and the renewal and modernisation of vessels in these regions is therefore an important element in ensuring good working conditions for our fishermen. the amendment therefore proposes raising the a-rate or the union's share to 50% and the c-rate or the share of other national or regional contributions to 40%. that is the amendment to this report which i consider essential. there is a second amendment, mrs mckenna's amendment no 6, which is not a problem. it consists of indicating in the report that these adaptations and developments must not be exploited to feed the flags of convenience system; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. finally, there are amendments nos 7 and 8, which raise the question of non-retroactivity. this question was raised at the meeting of the committee on fisheries. the commission has not been very clear. she was even hesitant, not to mention she didn't respond in her answer. the amendment is still on the agenda, having been tabled again. the opinion of the regional committee is positive, as is that of the committee on agriculture. the committee on fisheries did not initially give a favourable opinion, at least not entirely, considering that this principle of non-retroactivity was a fundamental principle of our community legislation. but since the other two committees have given a favourable opinion and the european commission has not been very clear, i suggest that you give a favourable opinion. if legally this proved to be totally impossible, the law would settle the matter. if it is possible, it will have to be done, and in that case we will have decided in favour of a very good cause.

in writing. - we voted for the limitation of working time and driving time for so-called independent drivers, a category whose existence has so far been one of the ways of circumventing the law in this field. we also object to the fact that break times are excluded from working time, whereas the driver is not in a position to use this time as he sees fit. it is also unacceptable that after stating that 'if night work is carried out, the daily working time does not exceed 8 hours for each 24-hour period', it is immediately added that this duration can be increased to 10 hours, provided that the average of 8 hours is respected over a longer reference period. it is unacceptable to calculate the working time "on average" because the accumulated fatigue, on a given day, beyond 8 hours is not mitigated by the monthly or annual average, with the risks this implies for the safety of the driver and other road users.
in writing. - this report is a first step, timid as it may be, but a first step which is very necessary to regulate the road transport sector, where there is maximum exploitation of employed and selfemployed drivers and where, like maritime transport, a genuine complacency system is being set up: company headquarters outside the european union, truck fleets and crews outside all the standards and conventions of labour law. europe must move towards improving existing legislation, including the revision of regulation 3820/85, and towards aligning it with the best achievements of union workers with regard to working time and night work. no country or company should be excluded from the directive, no derogation should be granted. to enforce the legislation, the european union must have the necessary human and financial resources, including the hiring of a sufficient number of qualified labour inspectors and controllers. at present, a driver's working time can be as long as 60 to 70 hours, of which at least 50 hours are spent behind the wheel. working time is not only driving time but also all other operations. night work must be drastically reduced - 8 hours of driving is still too long - with corresponding compensation and it must be limited to certain goods carried. finally, selfemployed road haulage operators must be subject to the same regulations as other employees. we have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the aim of this directive is to improve the identification of vessels bound for european ports and the monitoring of all vessels transiting through high-traffic or dangerous areas, and to oblige these vessels to be equipped with transponder systems enabling them to be automatically identified and continuously monitored by the coastal authorities. again, we can see that this directive has made clear progress in terms of control, but it has important shortcomings, particularly with regard to crews. it is unacceptable that, in the face of the well-known plight of seafarers on many ships at risk, the examination of the health and physical condition of the crew should not be part of the compulsory inspections. similarly, inspections must be carried out by trained personnel in sufficient numbers. finally, the concept of a "port of refuge" will only be real if effective facilities exist for these shelters. we shall vote for this directive while continuing to work to ensure that men (seamen, inspectors) are finally considered in their rightful place: the first!
in writing. - while we abstain on the mastorakis report establishing a european maritime safety agency, we will vote for the sterckx report because it provides for concrete measures to limit the risks of pollution and the endangerment of the lives of crew. it should be stressed, however, that it took disasters, in particular those caused by the oil tanker erika and then by the sinking of the chemical tanker ievoli sun, before measures were finally proposed. these measures remain in force. in particular, nothing is proposed to make these measures mandatory for ship owners and contractors alike. the minimum that can be done is to hold both parties responsible for any breach of these directives in respect of their other property.
in writing. - this draft regulation, if adopted, will allow the creation of a european maritime safety agency. as far as maritime safety is concerned, it does indeed seem appropriate to deal with the issue at european level. the agency will be used to coordinate training, scientific and technical assistance to member states for the application of legislation, the collection of data on marine pollution, monitoring and possible proposals for changes to existing legislation. it is a tool that does not interfere with the political decisions of states but helps in decision-making and control. the agency is also desired by almost all the actors in the marine environment. nevertheless, the commission's role in appointing the president and the members of the administrative board and in managing the agency is so important that citizens who have called for the creation of this agency risk being left out. that is why we are proposing several amendments to correct the original proposal. it is perfectly legitimate for members of parliament, local elected representatives, associations for the protection of seafarers' rights and environmental protection to be part of the agency's board of directors. it is also legitimate for the commission to report regularly on the results of its work.
in writing. - this regulation will allow the establishment of a fund for compensation for damage caused by oil pollution in european waters. the flood of december 1999 once again exposed the inadequacy of compensation: most victims have still not been compensated. the proposal is a definite improvement. however, it is insufficient because it does not go to the end of the logic of the shipowner-charterer duo. it is an improvement, because the financing of the fund will be provided by european companies, which will allow for a quick and substantial compensation. it is a regulation which has major shortcomings, since it does not establish unlimited liability for polluters and does not require that all damage caused be paid. that is why we are tabled amendments. some of them aim to establish unlimited liability by clearly establishing the link between the owner of the ship and the flag state and by requiring shipowners and ship-owners to take out unlimited insurance. others are trying to increase transparency in the management of the cope fund through the composition of its committee. we will vote in favour of this text, but we will continue to work to ensure that the total damage is financed by the colossal profits of the polluters.
in writing. - i should like to focus my remarks on the question of compensation for victims of oil pollution, which our assembly has rightly proposed to extend to pollution by dangerous products. the current system of limiting the financial liability of shipowners (which is scandalous in itself) and of self-limitation of the liability of oil charterers (in the framework of a fipol with capped resources and unrelated to the real cost of the pollution caused) results in tragically inadequate coverage of the damage caused to victims. it is unacceptable that the victims, or more generally the taxpayers, should be forced to substitute themselves financially for those responsible for the act of pollution. the commission therefore proposes the creation of a specifically european fund (cope) operating on the principle of member states' subrogation to the parties involved in oil pollution actions. but the responsibility of each actor, and of course first and foremost that of the shipowner and the charterer, must be clearly identified and clearly imputed to the victims. we agree on the objectives: that victims should be compensated for the full extent of the harm suffered and that compensation mechanisms should operate efficiently and swiftly. on the other hand, we are concerned about the proposed arrangements for the operation of the cope fund and in particular about the alignment of the cope procedures with the fipol procedures. in these circumstances, victims may face the same difficulties as, for example, the erika victims, namely the problems of proof of pollution and refusal of payment by companies. the commission is therefore proposing that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.
in writing. - under the pretext of helping kosovo, this report proposes to help the privatisation of the country's economy, which means, according to the examples cited in the text itself, subjecting it to western banks. our vote against expresses our indignation at the whole policy pursued by the western powers, particularly those of the european union. the policy of the european union is to make the ruin of both kosovo and serbia an additional outlet for western capital. it would be the least of their problems for the western powers to repair what they have destroyed. only a fraction of the money spent on the war, a fraction of the resources and technology deployed, would be sufficient to repair infrastructure, to rebuild roads, railways and telephone lines, and to rebuild destroyed buildings and businesses. this should be done at the expense of the western powers, more precisely their military budgets, and without generating any private profit in the west. for the moment, despite the self-congratulations, the economic balance sheet of the european union's intervention is reduced to the dismemberment of what remains of kosovo's economy and its subordination to western banks and the rule of the mafias.
in writing. - we would be unreserved in aiding overseas countries which centuries of colonization and exploitation by european countries have kept in an economically underdeveloped position. we are, however, concerned about the way the european union conceives its aid to these regions, which it calls 'ultra-peripheral', insofar as it is not intended solely for the poor, workers and small farmers, but also for the support of interests, indigenous or not, which have no need for it, and in addition to promoting 'entrepreneurship'. we are for aid but on other conditions. we therefore abstained, but voted in favour of amendments which might be in the interests of the working classes.
in writing. - the report notes in its recital that 'high oil prices and fluctuations affect mainly the most vulnerable sections of the population'. the explanatory memorandum also states that the increases are mainly the result of speculation. but all the rest is evidence of the willful impotence of the european institutions, as well as of the national states, to intervene. each speculative price increase is a huge levy levied by a few oil companies and capitalist intermediaries on the population, including the poorest layers who pay directly or indirectly. as for the governments, not only do they not intervene to curb these increases, but they profit from them through oil taxes, an indirect tax that is as unfair as vat because it hits the richest and the poorest in the same way. it is not true that the public authorities cannot prohibit price increases. it is not true that they cannot remove the tax on petroleum products for personal consumption. the commission is unable to take the necessary measures and is content to line up empty phrases. we therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - it is important that member states give serious consideration to reducing their dependence on energy supplies from outside the european union. on the one hand, for strategic reasons, which will become more acute as oil becomes scarcer, more expensive and more localized in one region of the world, and not necessarily the most democratic. on the other hand, the problem of climate change linked to the greenhouse effect has forced us to respect international commitments. this is why member states must do everything possible to reduce their consumption of fossil fuels. one of the ways we can do this is by developing biofuels. it has not been sufficiently taken into account in the european commission's proposals: we have the possibility of producing large quantities of oilseeds, sugar beet and cereals which can produce millions of hectolitres of fuel to replace fossil fuels. the most knowledgeable people in the automobile and oil industries are supporting this strategy. we therefore believe that the member states and the commission must do everything possible to facilitate research, development and productive investment in biofuels, in particular by means of appropriate tax measures: it is urgent that the member states understand that biofuels should not be subject to the taxes that affect fossil oil products.
mr president, the situation in the central african republic has just deteriorated again, and several hundred people have been killed in the aftermath of the attempted coup and the repression that followed. this crisis is striking once again a population that is the victim of tribal strife in a country that has suffered for decades from a serious economic crisis, as our colleague mr haarder has just reminded us. it is all the more worrying because it has led to the intervention of foreign armed forces and militias in the country, as happened in the democratic republic of congo. it is a risk that the central african republic will be plunged into a similar chaos, generating ever greater misery. the european union cannot turn a blind eye to this tragedy. it is not a question of returning to a policy of interference. it is a matter of not giving in to the temptation of indifference. the resolution which will be put to the vote in this house shortly expresses our sympathy and condemns the return to violence. the european union has a duty to do more by increasing humanitarian aid, of course, and above all by closely associating itself with the efforts of the united nations to create a climate of reconciliation which, in my view, would be greatly facilitated by the deployment in the country of a peacekeeping force, similar to the one that had played a beneficial role between 1998 and last february. we refer to this in our motion for a resolution, which the group of the european people's party and the european democrats will support unreservedly.
- mr president, we support the adoption of this resolution which denounces the repression by the central african army after the coup attempt of 28 may and the ethnic character of this repression. the resolution, however, in its first recital, expresses concern at the non-repayment of debts to the world bank by one of the poorest countries in the world and by a population that is starving. the resolution denounces the presence of foreign armed forces, in this case libyan. but how can we not remember that the foreign armed force that has been present in this country for the longest time, that has marked its fate in evil, is the french army? it was the french army that protected colonial rule, and then it was the french army that placed one of its junior officers, bokassa, as head of the independent central african state, without asking the opinion of the population. how can we forget the protection granted for years to the dictator bokassa and his thugs, the presence of french ministers and the president himself at the masquerade of bokassa's self-crowned emperor? we therefore condemn the leaders of the central african republic and its army, but we would like to remind the french state of its much greater responsibility and we will abstain on the resolution.
commission. – mr president, the commission is concerned about the recent attempted coup in the central african republic and the increasing political and social instability in the country. in this context, the commission, together with the central african republic, has recently finalised a country support strategy aimed at promoting good governance and a more stable, social and institutional environment as prerequisites for sustainable development. the community's cooperation is to be focused on the transport and health sectors. this strategy may have to be reviewed in the light of recent events. it should be emphasised that the crisis did not turn at any time into a widespread mutiny and remained essentially confined to military operations. the resulting humanitarian crisis appears to be well identified and manageable. the commission's humanitarian aid office (echo) has, since the beginning of the crisis, been in regular contact with the delegation and international ngos coordinating with the un on the ground in bangui. in consultation with these partners, and in response to this crisis, the commission will be providing up to eur 1 million for a two-month operation. this will include emergency food aid for 35 000 children and other particularly vulnerable groups, such as pregnant women and the elderly; medical assistance in the form of drugs, medical equipment and small-scale rehabilitation to enable looted health centres to reopen immediately; and reinstallation assistance in the form of basic household items and, possibly, support to refurbish badly damaged homes.

commission. – thank you, honourable members. i wish to thank the rapporteur, mrs redondo jiménez and the agriculture committee for the report on the proposal for a council directive on community measures for the control of classical swine fever. the main purpose of the commission proposal is to update the existing control provisions on swine fever, so as to take into account the most recent knowledge and experience acquired in controlling its agent. the proposal also takes account of the development of new diagnostic tools and vaccines, and of the opinions given by the scientific committee on these issues. this house is well aware that in 1997/1998, a major outbreak of classical swine fever occurred in several member states. this crisis led the commission to review community legislation on this issue and to look at the possibility of introducing provisions on the use of the so-called marker vaccines as an additional tool against the disease in case of emergency. the urgency for this review has been added to by the worrying outbreak in the united kingdom last year, and today there is confirmation of an outbreak in the region of lérida in catalonia, spain. the commission has immediately taken a decision, in full consultation with the spanish authorities, to impose restrictions on exports from this region. this decision will be reviewed at a meeting of the standing veterinary committee, scheduled for this week. the decision taken today has immediate effect until 30 june and will be reviewed in the meantime. before standing up in this debate, i had a brief telephone conversation on this matter with the spanish minister for agriculture. a single farm is concerned, and i am happy to say that he informed me that all of the animals moved from that farm before confirmation had been slaughtered. however, we must remain particularly vigilant in relation to this issue. the situation will need to be followed up very closely, and i will be happy to keep parliament informed of developments. returning to the current proposal, and marker vaccination in particular, the commission financed specific trials and research projects. by means of this research very valuable information was obtained. it has been essential for the commission in drawing up its proposal and cautiously paving the way for the potential use of these vaccines. clearly, their use can only be envisaged in an emergency situation and once laboratory tests are available to discriminate between vaccinated and infected animals. here i must emphasise the importance of the efficacy of the tests, as distinct from the marker vaccinations themselves. encouragingly, parliament's agriculture committee, the economic and social committee, the committee of the regions and the member states, largely support the commission's approach to this sensitive issue. this contrasts with the situation a few years ago, when quite different opinions were expressed by the experts themselves. this reminds us of the importance of scientific investigation, so that informed answers can be given to technically complex matters such as this. indeed, i am aware that in preparing her report, mrs redondo organised an interesting and important hearing in the agricultural committee attended by swine fever experts from different member states to better understand the progress made on this issue after the outbreak from 1997/1998. the report of madame redondo largely supports the main aspects of the commission proposal and of course, i am obviously very pleased about this. however, allow me to address in detail the amendments, which have been proposed. i will begin with the amendments the commission cannot accept. the commission cannot accept amendments nos 2 to 5, 26, 28 and 30, as they go beyond the scope of this directive. i understand that the recent fmd crisis has prompted parliament to raise some horizontal problems related to animal health, which certainly need to be addressed. the report deals for example with the implementation of controls on imports of live animals and products, traceability, financing of costs related to animal diseases and future animal health problems, which may emerge in relation to enlargement. i share the concern of the parliament. but these complex issues cannot be addressed in this directive. i have already informed this assembly that the commission will address those issues before the end of the year in a separate legal framework. the commission cannot accept amendments nos 6 to 8, 12, 16 to 18, 22, 24, 25 and 29, which contain certain technical details of relatively minor importance, for which the commission considers the text of its proposal more suitable. amendment no 15 concerns the establishment of community financed market support measures, in case of prolonged standstill of pigs in holdings kept under movement restrictions due to an outbreak of swine fever. the commission cannot accept this amendment, as such decisions must be taken on a case-by-case basis. the legal basis for doing so already exists in the framework of the common market organisation for pig meat. this mechanism demonstrated its efficiency and there is no need for further legal provisions in this regard. amendments nos 20 and 21 concern the role of different authorities in the control of classical swine fever in wild boar. the commission cannot accept these amendments, as it is for the member states to ensure that all authorities potentially involved in the control of the disease are given a proper role. their co-ordination must be guaranteed to ensure proper eradication. amendment no 23 concerns the introduction of an article on the potential use of marker vaccines. as i have already said, the commission and parliament agree on this important issue. the commission however cannot accept this amendment, as its proposal already includes comprehensive provisions on marker vaccines. however, we will take into account parliament's remarks in a new recital. amendments nos 20 and 29 concern the legal status of the classical swine fever diagnostic manual, which the commission intends to adopt. after the adoption of this directive, following the opinion of the standing veterinary committee, the report suggests including this manual as part of the directive itself. the commission feels that this could create confusion from a legal point of view and thus cannot accept these amendments. however, some modifications will be introduced in the text to reinforce the concept but the manual must be an essential part of community legislation on swine fever. amendments nos 24 and 25 note the need for some transitional provisions on contingency plans, which are indeed already in article 28 of the proposal. while the commission shares the views of the parliament, it cannot accept these amendments. on the other hand, the commission can accept entirely or partially, a number of amendments. in these cases, drafting changes are also needed. these concern not only some technical aspects of the directive, like disinfection of holdings, or other contaminated materials and sampling of suspected pigs, but also some more substantial and sensitive issues, like marker vaccination and the introduction of a ban on feeding pigs with catering waste. on this last issue, i can only add to what i have already said in this chamber last tuesday, during the debate on the regulation of animal by-products, that the commission is committed to ensure consistency between this directive and that regulation. in summary, the commission can accept the following amendments in full or in part and subject to necessary drafting changes: amendments nos 1, 9-11, 14, 19, 27, 31 and 32. the commission cannot accept amendments nos 2-8, 12, 13, 15-18, 20-26, 28-30 and 33-37. to conclude, ladies and gentlemen, i wish once again to thank madam redondo and the agriculture committee for the excellent report and their support.
- thank you, chief. the debate is closed. the vote will take place at 6.30 p.m.
- doc. a5-0192/2001 by mr pérez royo, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on the proposal for a council regulation on the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial compensation provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the islamic federal republic of the comoros on fishing off the comoros for the period 28 february 2001 to 27 february 2004 (com (2001) 173 - c5-0144/2001 - 2001/0088 (cns)).
the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. i should like to begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr pérez royo, for his report on the new fisheries protocol with the comoros. i am also pleased that you, mr rapporteur, fully support this proposal. the new protocol concerns tuna only and provides for fishing opportunities for a total of 65 vessels, as has already been said. the financial contribution is approximately eur 350 000 per year. it is also welcome that 60% of this sum will be used for targeted measures to develop the local fisheries sector in the comoros, with particular attention to small-scale fisheries. i shall now turn to the amendments. amendments nos 1, 3 and 4 are not a problem in terms of content, but in our view they are superfluous because the commission already meets the requirements contained in the amendments in the framework of the interinstitutional agreements and in particular the framework agreement between the european parliament and the commission of 5 july last year. i am sorry to say that i cannot agree to amendment no 5. the principle in this case is that a new mandate is not required for a protocol to be renegotiated, since it is an annex to an agreement. i can fully support amendment no 2, but we do not think that it is necessary either, because the principles it deals with are already in line with the community's fundamental position on sustainable and responsible fishing. i would like to mention our communication on fisheries and poverty reduction and the recently presented green paper on the future of fisheries policy. as regards amendment no 6, the commission shares parliament's concern with regard to the protection of the habitat of the comorian quail. instead of mentioning this in the text of the council regulation, i propose the following procedure: the commission is prepared to write to the comorian authorities to convince them of the importance of this species and the problem it poses. we shall then be happy to send a copy of this letter to the chairman of the committee on fisheries, mr varela. i cannot accept amendment no 7. it is an integral part of our agreement policy and it is also stated in all the negotiating directives that the financial compensation for the fishing rights granted must be partly borne by the eu budget and partly by the shipowners. in concrete terms, this means that the community will pay the financial compensation to the third country concerned, but ship owners will clearly have to pay the licence fees themselves.

- the next item is the report (a5-0235/2001) by mr zimmerling, on behalf of parliament's delegation to the conciliation committee, on the joint text approved by the conciliation committee for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the right of succession for the author of an original work of art (c5-0220/2001 - 1996/0085 (cod)).
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the agreement reached by our rapporteur, mr zimmerling, is a compromise agreement on a very interesting matter. it has been criticised by some artists' groups who have told us that they think that, paradoxically, the new directive would be an unacceptable injustice between famous and struggling artists, that it would provide no support to artists who need it most. we are being told that there is a distortion between a privileged minority of artists, whose works are sold in art galleries and auction houses, and the majority of artists, who are officially denied the right of succession because their works are traded between individuals or sold to museums by private collectors. in reality, it is conceivable that the threshold for the application of the right of succession was the subject of lengthy discussions: between eur 1 000 and eur 4 000, a compromise was reached on the sum of eur 3 000, which is a reasonable amount. more worrying, however, is the derogation from the rule of equality before the law, which may give rise to appeals before the luxembourg court, resulting in particular from the late date of entry into force of the directive for the states which, until now, have not known the right of succession: i am talking about the date of 2010. in any event, there is a danger that the right of succession itself - which certainly shows how it responds to laudable concerns - will, as the previous speaker has said, create a bureaucracy which is more likely to paralyse the art market than to bring legitimate satisfaction to the current creators.
- the agenda calls for a joint debate on: - the report of the european council and the commission statement on the european council meeting of 15 and 16 june 2001 in gothenburg; - the statement by the presidency-in-office of the council on the balance sheet of the swedish presidency. i have the pleasure of giving the floor to the president-in-office of the council, mr persson.
- madam president, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, in gothenburg there was a lot of talk about 'sustainable development', a nebulous concept, but a trend. it is no doubt to be welcomed that the member states are willing to introduce public health and environmental concerns into all policies imposed by brussels. after the mad cow and the foot and mouth disease, let's just say it was high time. the insistence on presenting the kyoto protocol and the future global pact as the panacea is, on the other hand, a travesty. it is a market for dupes whose only customer is europe, a sort of new whiteness of the white man who is accused of degrading the planet all by himself. neither china nor india will participate, because they are the ones who favor development, growth and industrialization. the same is true of the us, where growth is slowing down in the face of increased international competition. secondly, you cannot find words strong enough to condemn the violent demonstrations that took place during the summit. it is a pity that these expressions of indignation are forgotten when it comes to condemning the daily violence and insecurity that millions of our fellow citizens are subjected to. the european governments - and french in particular - are not even able to protect their own people. their immigration policy, the culture of excuses, the defence of the rights of thugs in the name of human rights, the abolition of the death penalty are all factors that are criminogenic. rather than pointing the finger at a handful of leftists, who were curiously dubbed fascists by mr crespo - unless mr crespo wanted to acknowledge that fascism had indeed its origins in socialism, all its leaders having been socialist leaders before becoming fascist leaders. finally, it is scandalous that no one is offended by the totalitarian drift of the european institutions. it is only here that people are systematically forced to return to the polls when the result of an election is unpleasant. under threat, denmark gave in in 1992; austria rightly refused to do so. the irish must resist: their 'no', in law and in fact, is the final straw for the treaty of nice. all the nations that have not been consulted - and who will not be for fear of their negative answer - are in solidarity with them.
- madam president, mr president, what we will remember from the swedish presidency is that, unfortunately, for the first time since the birth of the european communities, police officers, who were europeans in this instance, fired live ammunition at european demonstrators. what we will get from the swedish presidency is this violence and this contempt. the contempt with which european leaders have treated the result of the referendum in ireland. the gothenburg summit showed that the european union is becoming a kind of 'forbidden city', as alien to the european peoples and as contemptuous of them as the manchu dynasty was of the most distant of the mongolian peoples. it seems to me that the european union is reproducing, and i know this may be shocking, a colonial mode of operation vis-à-vis the nations that make up it, with the exception that the colonial power here intends to proceed with colonization instead of preceding it, as has been the case in history. the irish people, a people long scarred by history, have therefore reacted in a way that seems to me to herald a general upheaval among the peoples of europe: to face the emergence of a new kind of neo-colonialism, something that has been endemic since maastricht, amsterdam and now nice, which claims to rule over them and to bring them the benefits of a company that is essentially a health-giving enterprise, europe.
- mr president, the gothenburg council was on the right track when it confirmed that the enlargement process is irreversible and set the objective of bringing the first candidate countries into the eu in time to enable them to take part in the 2004 european elections. but at the same time, the council made a serious mistake when, in paragraph 4 of its conclusions, it seemed to link the fate of enlargement to that of the treaty of nice. it is a legal, political and moral mistake. the legal problem is that, as the president of the commission said on 21 june - and perhaps that is why the president of the commission, mr poettering, is not here today - 'legally, the ratification of the treaty of nice is not necessary for enlargement'. i shall not go into that again, because, from a legal point of view, mr prodi has not been denied by anyone since. secondly, it is a political mistake, because the treaty of nice is politically indispensable to enlargement only for those who want to build a european 'superstate'. they want to link the superstate, european enlargement and the treaty of nice, at the risk of destroying them all together. finally, there is a moral fault, because by confirming the declaration of the general affairs council of 11 june, the gothenburg council showed a profound contempt for the democratic expression of a people, which casts a strange light on the europe it wants to build. we want to welcome the eastern countries into a democratic and free europe, and that is why, mr president, we support the irish people's lucid and courageous choice.
- mr president, in gothenburg the european council took two contradictory decisions. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting. - i 'm good . on the other hand, and at the same time, the heads of state and government have decided to ignore the consequences of the irish 'no' vote in the last referendum. this 'no' creates major uncertainty about the timing of ratification, and perhaps even its outcome. the ratification of nice now requires that the irish national elections take place, that those elections lead to the victory in dublin of a majority more united than the current majority on the subject, and of a majority ready to commit its credibility on this now undermined ground. and the new leaders must find arguments that convince the irish people to change their minds. those who now tell us that this will be a mere formality are the same people who were asleep before the recent referendum. this means that for the applicant countries the treaty of nice is no longer the sesame on the doorstep of the union, it has become a lock, a lock that has been closed by the irish and there is no guarantee that it will be reopened. the only guarantee that the timetable promised in gothenburg will be met is to start accession negotiations on the basis of the current treaties, i.e. the treaty of amsterdam. that's what mr. prodi tried to say and he was silenced. but the politics of the ostrich are not good counsel. with or without nice, institutional reform is still a long way off. the european parliament now considers that it can only be achieved by a constitutional approach. but in the meantime, the language of truth obliges us to tell the applicant countries that they have no other guarantee of keeping to the proposed timetable than to start negotiating on the basis of amsterdam. if the treaty of nice is finally ratified in the autumn of 2002, it will still be time to join it. otherwise, the enlargement will be saved.
in writing. - if this report had really been aimed at improving the legal protection of accident victims, as it claims, we would have voted for it. but even if the recommendations accompanying the report contain some proposals which would make it a little easier for the injured parties, in the end it is a laborious juggling act in order not to harm the interests of the insurance companies in any way. for example, in this europe that claims to be united, insurance companies will be allowed to charge an additional premium to their insured persons who temporarily move to another state of the european union. the big claims about european unity are dwarfed by a small surprise... we therefore abstained on this report.

- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is time, six months before the fateful date, to consider how the citizens will experience the disappearance of their national currency. last to be consulted, they are also the last to be informed. the most 'europeanist' readers of mr maaten's report will feel a sudden anxiety rising within them: almost total unpreparedness, the euro's infrequent or even marginal use in international transactions, including intra-european transactions, doubt about the possibility for citizens to change their coins free of charge in banks, aberrant pricing of cross-border transactions, even though they are carried out in the same currency, abusive price increases which will certainly be the occasion for a change of currency. the litany is long and it's not cheerful. the euro, which was demanded by governments for ideological reasons and by big financial interests for reasons of their own interest, has not succeeded in winning over even its most ardent supporters in the two years since it was introduced, let alone on international markets. the euro has lost value against the dollar with no sign of recovery anytime soon. the changeover to the euro in cash is therefore probably a useless, costly operation, generating inflation and public or private embezzlement. it's better to stop while there's still time.
- mr president, the randzio-plath report, like the european central bank's annual report for the financial year 2000, repeats the usual assertion that the euro would make a decisive contribution to the stability of the area by making it less vulnerable to external shocks. it's the old shield theory. but it now appears to be only marginally true, by eliminating fluctuations in exchange rates between member countries. on the other hand, and this is more serious, the euro is not currently acting as a shield but as an amplifier of the crisis caused by the spread of the us slowdown, since it prevents each country from deploying a response adapted to its specificity. chancellor schröder has just called on the ecb to take up its responsibilities in supporting growth in germany. he is wrong, and he should realise that he is a victim of the monetary union rule of the game. the ecb can hardly reduce its interest rates drastically to satisfy germany, because other countries are expressing contrary demands. and, incidentally, a fall in interest rates could cause the euro to fall even further, which would have a very bad effect on the eve of the physical exchange of coins and notes. it seems, mr president, that europeans are likely to pay a heavy price for wanting the single currency with different economies, and this is all the more so as the euro itself, according to the latest figures available, seems to be contributing to increasing divergences, both in terms of inflation and growth.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall now turn to the difficulties which people in my country complain about every day. it is indeed curious to say the least that the coué method, which prevailed in creating the euro, has now given way to the forte method. i regret to say that the move to the single currency seems to me to be a very strong move. at first, the peoples were not consulted at any time to find out whether they were in favour of replacing their national currency. the irish example is, in this respect, symptomatic of the way our europe works. the people are no longer consulted on the practical implementation of the euro, even though they are the centrepieces of this chessboard. the information campaigns carried out by politicians are always blaming the citizens. understand this: if the euro fails, it will be your fault. young people and pensioners have an informative function, and administrations and their civil servants are examples. finally, the shopkeepers are the practical trainers. for example, who cares about the difficulties faced by traders in rural areas, far from the training centres in the cities? how can you ask a trader who works 12 hours a day to go to his chamber of commerce or trades to take part in information meetings? in conclusion, and for all these reasons, i do not think it is right to leave all the responsibility to the citizens. it is too easy to blame others for what we are unable to do ourselves. europe wanted a single currency, now let it take it on!
mr president, the directive drawn up by the commission is totally biased. what interests him is the promotion of supplementary pensions by capitalisation. the karas report sometimes corrects this bias, but sometimes it also makes it worse. we are faced with a reference model which is above all that of the supplementary pension industry in britain and elsewhere. in some countries, however, these organisations do not go to the financial market, or very little of it. in other countries, strong guarantees are offered to workers, but this is clearly not the aim of the directive. in particular, it is not interested in the coherence of pension systems built up in the national space on the principles of solidarity, security and universality. that is why we tabled amendments on two fronts: on the one hand, the guarantees for the populations concerned, and on the other, public control and prudential behaviour. the text seems unacceptable to us in the absence of substantial improvements. first, we must improve the guarantees for the people. the directive carries risks of discrimination and a breakdown in solidarity. membership of a supplementary scheme is not compulsory, which leads to considerable inequalities. cross-sectoral mutualisations are not provided for. any deterioration in demography would lead to a decline in the quality of services. changes in job or sector for mobile workers are not covered by continuity guarantees. the definition of rights does not necessarily include biometric risks. the guarantees of effective benefits are not organised. and we know the risks involved in subscribing to defined contribution schemes, as many well-known macroeconomists have shown. we are proposing amendments on all these points, as well as on the second point of concern: the necessary improvement of social and prudential control. the commission offers insurers the choice of opting for occupational pension schemes. the karas report reinforces this provision by excluding public authorization. this opens the door to competition, with two risks: diversion of solidarity missions and weakening of the prudential regimes imposed on insurers. mr karas has incorporated our amendment to establish the principle of participatory management, but this will only have real effect if the institutions concerned are not treated as financial investors like the others throughout the directive. the commission's prudential framework is vague and the report imposes the principle of the country of origin, which is unacceptable to us, because the host countries must also, of course, retain the possibility of establishing consistency with domestic social law. finally, the prior tax harmonization is still absent from these texts, so that once again the door is opened to tax dumping. ladies and gentlemen, today we are faced with a key test of how the european parliament conceives its responsibilities in the field of social protection.
- this report contains prejudices which may be nothing but stupid but which, moreover, serve as a justification for reducing the amount of pensions and extending the working week. the argument from demographics and what the report calls "longer life expectancy associated with lower birth rates" becomes false if the substantial increase in labour productivity is concealed at the same time. given the increase in the productivity of each worker, the same number of active workers produces more than enough not only to make possible the growth of their own living standards but also to provide a decent pension for three or four times as many pensioners as a quarter of a century ago. if this increase in production capacity were not entirely diverted to the benefit of a privileged minority, society could ensure that all pensioners were paid a full salary without being forced to work longer. your economy is turning everything into a commodity, including the pensions you want to deliver to the sharks of finance, but, by the same token, it is the retired working class worn out from work that you are turning into a commodity, and that is despicable. the failure to provide material security for the elderly is one of the most striking manifestations of a decadent social organization.

- madam president, mr president of the council, mr president of the commission, i appreciated the fact that you, mr president of the council, frankly acknowledged what you rightly called 'a crisis of european identity' between our fellow citizens and the european union, and that you stressed the need to take seriously their aspirations in order to - as you said - reconcile citizens with europe. this is a change from the too frequent, lenient speeches which, by smoothing out all contradictions, become inaudible to people. what could be more normal than to see the emergence of new questions from life experience, which call for adaptations, innovations and, sometimes, questioning of what we thought was taken for granted. no subject should be taboo: the problems must be recognised, you stressed. in this context, let me mention some of the issues that are coming up more and more frequently in the debate on the economic upheaval that is also affecting the european union. these questions have, in my view, their place in the great debate you wish to promote during your presidency. we have been told, for example, that the euro zone is essentially protected from the fallout of the us economic downturn. it is clear that this is not the case. that is a diagnostic error that is not a minor one. what do we do with it ? what lessons can be drawn from this in the field of economic and monetary policy so that the european economy is less involved in the american financial bubble, which is now bursting? i would remind you that the flow of european capital to the united states has increased ninefold in the last six years, to over 220 billion dollars last year. another example, which mr duisenberg himself mentions on occasion, is that, unlike the us federal reserve, whose mandate is to act in favour of employment and growth, the european central bank has not been given the task of dealing with these problems, which are the heart of all concerns. do the europeans know ? and what exactly do they think about it at the very moment when unemployment is rising and growth is falling? are there any questions to be asked about this? another example: the fiscal stability pact requires states to pursue a policy of rationing public and social expenditure. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. what revision of the usual criteria or their implementation can be envisaged to overcome this contradiction? in general, the fundamental question which the new economic situation - which is deteriorating rapidly - raises and imposes on us is, in my view, this: how much political creativity are we capable of developing to avoid serious tensions in each of our societies, or even between some of our states and, even more so, with the candidate countries? the answer to this question cannot be found in a project such as the election of the president of the commission by universal suffrage. i think we will have to tackle the hard core of the neoliberal model, which is too much a part of our european construction, and we will have to not only listen but also involve the social actors and citizens in this necessary change. i would like to know, mr president-in-office, how far the audacity and courage of the belgian presidency which you are inaugurating today reaches in this respect.
- mr president-in-office of the council, in your speech you said that you wanted to reconcile europe and its peoples. the gap is widening today and you will have a lot of work to do to close it, especially after the disastrous effect of the gothenburg council's disregard for the democratic expression of the irish people. unfortunately, the advanced federalism which you advocate, with a certain audacity, it must be said, for a presidency which will have to seek consensus, this federalism can only distance europe from its peoples. what would it take to reconnect? first, of course, respect for national democracies. we regret that the recent benelux memorandum on the future of the union contains absolutely nothing on this respect. we want a europe which respects its peoples in practice and, first of all, we ask that the next intergovernmental conference be prepared by the national parliaments and by them alone, by excluding all the confused and illegitimate bodies or committees of so-called wise men, which only succeed in leading europe astray on paths without any exit. respect for national democracies also means avoiding projects which ignore national sovereignty, such as the european tax which you, mr president-in-office of the council, are pushing through by renaming it direct financing of the european budget. it is the national parliaments and only they who must have the power to approve the tax, because they are the ones who have the primary legitimacy. finally, to reconnect europe with its peoples means to listen to the citizens, something which was clearly not done when it was decided to make the euro not merely a complement to national currencies but a substitute which eliminates them by raising immense practical difficulties. it is a mistake, you will see by the end of the year, and to fix it, to re-establish the link with the people, we will need a better understanding of the concrete problems of the citizens and, no doubt, a great deal of flexibility.

in writing. the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy (ces) adopted a resolution on the proposal for a council directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the permissible sound power level of towed vehicles. the common position adopted in march differs considerably from the position adopted at first reading by parliament last november, even though the council accepted about a third of the amendments proposed by parliament. the rapporteur tried to secure a compromise before the second reading in the ep and explained to the committee that the council had, at the trilogue on tuesday 19 june, agreed to eight of the nine compromise amendments. the only unresolved issue is whether waste incineration should be considered as a renewable energy source. the council intends to include it. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. therefore, the incineration of unsorted household waste should not be encouraged by this directive or by any future support scheme for renewable energy sources. one of the most profound disagreements between the two legislative bodies is whether national renewable energy targets should be binding or merely indicative. parliament insisted in november on the need for binding targets, but the council opposed this. the compromise states that if member states have not made progress towards their national indicative targets, the commission will have to come forward with proposals which may include binding targets. the national indicative targets should be consistent with the overall indicative target of 12% of gross domestic energy consumption in 2010 coming from renewable energy sources. at the same time, the latter will have to account for an indicative share of 22.1% of total electricity consumption in the community. in writing. - the draft directive and the karas report on pension funds and supplementary schemes are a further attack on the existing pension systems in the european union. the karas report builds on the very liberal conclusions of the feira european council in approving the directive. its approach is based on minimum harmonisation of rules and an 'anglo-saxon' approach to regulation, which means that there are no precise rules for determining the commitments undertaken by pension funds. the directive responds to the demands of the british and dutch pension fund industry, which wants to be able to operate at european level with a single fund instead of different funds in each country. once again, the european union is submitting to the dictatorship of the single market, this time in the pension sector, with consequences that we know all too well: worsening inequalities between employees, financial markets and shareholders' control over retirement savings and increasing pressure from pension funds against salaried employment. instead of harmonising downwards and creating a single market in pensions, we should be setting up a system of solidarity and equality at european level. that is why we voted against the karas report and reject the draft directive.
in writing. - this report concerns a proposal for a regulation on the 'eu' top-level domain. the commission proposal responds to the requests made at the lisbon council (23-24 march 2000). the stockholm council (23-24 march 2001) reiterated the same wish, stating that 'the council will take, with the commission, the necessary measures to ensure that the tld is not used in the same way as the name of the domain name of the member state in which it is registered'. eu shall be made available to users as soon as possible.' this may sound a little barbaric and needs some explanation. this regulation is intended to be a general act establishing a framework for the establishment of an 'eu' register. the register should be contracted by both the commission and icann (internet corporation for assigned names and numbers). i would remind you that icann was created in october 1998 with the aim of countering the american hegemony in the management of the internet. this private, non-profit corporation is responsible for four key areas of the internet, including dns (domain name system) and the allocation of internet protocol address spaces. icann is governed by a 19-member board of directors. its directors and external members are chosen on the basis of geographical balance. icann also has four advisory committees, including the gac (governments committee), in which the european commission and the member states participate. i am very pleased that the european union has decided to become more involved in this body in order to play a key role in the international management of the internet and to strengthen the neutrality of icann. in the same vein, if the european union wants to assert itself in cyberspace, it must create a domain name like its member states. for example, national territories are recognised on the internet by domain names such as '.uk' or '.be'. such a creation would be a decisive factor in accelerating the development of the electronic economy and commerce in europe. i therefore thought it important to validate the good work done by the rapporteur.
