in writing. - for decades governments throughout europe have been closing railway lines to promote the interests of private companies in all forms of road transport, because of the tragic accidents in the mont blanc and gotthard tunnels and the enormous human and social cost of all the more "ordinary" accidents. today, road networks are on the verge of collapse, so some private capital is turning to railways for new profits, aided by the european institutions as well as national governments. neither the users nor the general public have any good to expect from the privatisation of public services. nor are the workers in this sector who denounce and fight privatisation and its damage to employment and working conditions. the rapporteur is certainly concerned about the damage of 'wild liberalisation' and envisages the possibility for local authorities to oppose it, but he is nonetheless among those who recognise privatisation as a fact, the dismantling of public services as inevitable, and who are only trying to regulate this process somewhat. we are in favour of the development of public transport both on the main international routes and on regional and local networks, and we do not want to support either directly or indirectly the dismantling of public services, because even if regulated, this dismantling is detrimental to users, to workers in the sector, and constitutes a serious social regression. that is why we did not vote for this report and we reiterate that public services everywhere must be designed and implemented to meet the needs of users, not to generate profits for private companies.
in writing. - the proposal clearly states that its objective is to develop competition in the field of transport supply. contrary to what has been repeatedly stated, there is every indication that, in the context of what is known as 'regulated' competition, this opening up of the market has not produced good results or improved the efficiency of services. quite the opposite. the general approach to liberalization is opposed to improving service for users, improving working conditions, respect for the environment, road safety and a land-use planning policy that is not imposed by market constraints. we are against any liberalization of transport, for its maintenance as a public service and for cooperation between public undertakings at european level. we are against any kind of misguided state aid to private operators who are not prepared to invest in the necessary infrastructure. moreover, we are in favour of the immediate renationalisation of all private railway lines and networks in europe and the renationalisation/municipalisation of urban and short-distance transport. the basic problem is that we cannot compromise with the logic of the market. when it is applied, it is to the detriment of another logic: that of public service. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. - the draft report before us is not acceptable as it stands. firstly, because it provides a confused answer to the fundamental questions of competition between european ports and financial transparency in the allocation of subsidies to them. but also, and above all, because the indiscriminate liberalization of all port services is a dangerous threat to safety, the environment and employment. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the application of the competition rules to the provision of services of general economic interest. the environment, because liberalisation does not allow it to be taken into account in a satisfactory way. on these two points, the report and the directive are in contradiction with the policy of strengthening 'maritime safety' and reducing environmental risks launched by the union in the wake of the erika disaster. finally, as regards employment, because the opening up of port services to competition - particularly those which use the most manpower, such as cargo handling - risks plunging european ports into a dangerous spiral of 'less is more' in the social sphere. such a drift would be unsustainable in areas which are often fragile or in employment areas already severely affected by industrial conversions. i cannot therefore support all the provisions which would open up all port services to competition without any compensation or safeguards. that is why i voted for all the amendments to exclude port services (pilot, handling, cargo handling) from the scope of the liberalisation proposed by the directive. since these amendments were not adopted, i voted against the report.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to thank both our rapporteur in the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, mr georg jarzembowski, and the whole of this committee for the quality of the work they have put before us. i am voting against this report for several reasons. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the negotiations. the piloting, because it is the only one of the intra-port services to have been recognised as a compulsory public service and as an activity requiring high attention to safety, is the only intra-port service which will continue to be controlled by the member states and is therefore excluded from the scope of the directive. but it is simply incomprehensible to me that the fishermen, for example, who provide a service of general interest recognized internationally, in particular by providing essential aid both for prevention in environmental protection and for the implementation of the best possible safety, should now be subject to competition. voting against this report is also, in my view, rejecting the liberalisation of ports, in other words, rejecting competition between ports, competition which can only have harmful and disastrous effects, both in terms of the quality of the services provided and the working conditions themselves. voting against this report is therefore a plea for greater cooperation between ports, it is a recognition that ports are a full and integral part of spatial planning and as such should not be subject to competition which could lead to their loss. the two main reasons why i did not vote in favour of this report are as follows.
in writing. - the proposal for liberalization of port services raises the question of the practical consequences which it may have. it seems to us totally inappropriate to want to open up to competition all port services of any kind, since a number of them, because of their particular obligations, have the character of a public service. the aim, beyond the national differences in the conception of the very concept of public service applied to port services, must be to ensure optimal security throughout the states, which they alone can define and frame through public service missions, by means of professional qualifications, limitations or a definition of their activities. the economic logic in favour of the user-users must in no way take precedence over safety in the broad sense, safety of persons, the environment or equipment. so, whether it be steering, handling or other services, we believe that this proposal should exclude all services which, according to the standards of each state, have the character of a public service. it is not, and we shall therefore vote against it.
in writing. - the rapporteur, mr jarzembowski, after having attacked public rail transport, is now attacking port services. the logic, always the same, is that the liberalization of telecommunications, transport, energy and the postal services is a direct consequence of these processes. the aim is to place the organising authorities, infrastructures and professionals performing public service missions under the yoke of the market, often in a public context. three hundred ports in the european union and all port activities such as cargo handling, steering, towing, mooring, embarkation and disembarkation services would be covered by this directive. however, a recent opinion poll, confirmed by the success of the dockers' strike on 6 november, shows that these proposals are overwhelmingly rejected by the port services. the long battle for amendments in the committee on transport has certainly made it possible for the time being for competition to take place not within ports but between ports. but these results are not satisfactory and because we demand the maintenance of public service obligations concerning safety, regularity, continuity, quality and price, the harmonization of the social rights of port workers with the most favourable regime and respect for the environment, we have rejected the jarzembowski report.
in writing. - the management of the site is a service of general interest recognised by the judgment of the court of justice of 18 june 1998. in this context, the port authority may require the handling of cargo to deal with any safety problem, without any obligation to pay. the management ensures that all ships have the same quality of service, thanks to a very thorough knowledge of the port in which it operates. the permanence of the service, the professional qualifications of the staff, the mastery of local specificities, the essential role played by the management in port and maritime security make this activity an essential and determining element of environmental protection. the deterioration of the merchant fleet as a whole and the increasingly evident over-exploitation of ships and crews which are often defective demonstrate how, in the years to come, the oarsmen will play a vital role because of their technical skills linked to a deep knowledge of their workplace. as such, the management, like the steering, must be excluded from the european directive, and that is why our green/alternative group voted in favour of amendments 66 and 67 to this report.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done on this very sensitive subject. unlike in the past, the divisions were not political but national, and the compromise reached was generally positive. this directive was necessary because the opening up of port services to competition must take place and european ports need european regulations for port services. if competition is to be fostered, it is essential that it be organised in a proper framework. however, the specificities of each activity must be taken into account. i am thinking in particular of piloting and handling, which for safety reasons must remain the responsibility of the port authority. this management mode works very well in france and even though these activities are open to competition in other european countries, i am in favour of their current exclusion from the scope of the directive. we are dealing with port services of general interest. if these services are kept within the scope of the directive, the concept of a port authority loses its meaning. on the other hand, as regards cargo handling, i support liberalisation because we are dealing with a service of a commercial nature and opening up to competition should mean additional jobs in ports. finally, i supported the provisions for greater transparency in financial relations between ports and member states. in the interests of legal certainty and fair competition between european ports, subsidies paid by national authorities must be subject to thorough checks.
in writing. - this report is in line with the policy of the european institutions, in that it emphasizes aid to employers under the pretext of research and aims to link research and private interests ever more closely, even if it sometimes disguises it as a trendy, whether ecological or regionalist, dress. nor is the report free from concessions to certain obscurantist ideas, religious or otherwise. the budget for the sixth framework programme imposes financial penalties on research units whose work is considered to be non-priority because it is unlikely to have cost-effective applications in the short or medium term for the private sector. the only reason we voted for this report is that we do not want to undermine certain research directions which it supports and which are in the direction of scientific, medical or technological progress, nor do we want to risk depriving public sector researchers of the funding they need. and we also adopted all the amendments which could represent progress compared to the present situation.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i have long supported research efforts at european level. i am therefore pleased that parliament has shown its willingness to create and develop this interdisciplinary and community area. in france, in particular, we are seeing a worrying decline in the number of researchers. because of disappointing national policies, the most talented often go abroad and only too rarely return. the system incorporated in this report, concerning the mobility of researchers and return assistance, will therefore, i hope, make up for the shortcomings of some governments. stimulating research also means ensuring an independent training policy, building on existing skills at european level. the legislator may have the task of regulating research, but the risk is that it will be confined to a very tight box. the europe of discovery must therefore be encouraged, and work on biotechnologies, which represent the future, should be encouraged. we must support both the european basic research which is at the heart of the competitiveness of our industries and the many projects undertaken by smes, whose contribution to discovery and innovation is well known. research also affects the daily lives of all europeans, and priority areas such as food security, the fight against major diseases and the improvement of public health show the willingness to link research and well-being. i also welcome the proposed support for the development of research into childhood diseases, an area where national policies have often failed. that is why i am waiting for the commission to publish proposals on paediatric medicines.
in writing. - as a member of the committee on industry and research and the temporary committee on human genetics (bioethics), i attached particular importance to this report in its two main aspects: - the conditions for supporting research in europe, and - the ethical framework within which the european parliament proposes to carry it out. as the amendments show, the main part of the debate was on the part relating to 'ethics' in biotechnology. since the majority of the votes allowed the exploitation of the human person by authorising the exploitation of human embryos, in this case conceived in the context of 'treatments of sterility' by in vitro fertilisation, to the detriment of the promotion of the integrity and dignity of the person, i consider that the ethical framework adopted at first reading, by the majority, gives a negative colour to the whole of the report, including the technical provisions. in summary, despite good technical provisions, the allegedly 'ethical' provisions harm the integrity of the report as a whole, by not respecting the human person.

- madam minister, commissioner, let us not deny our pleasure at hearing once again the sound of music in the streets of the afghan capital and a woman's voice on radio kabul. the sense of liberation hope is not soon replaced by a new nightmare. first of all, the fighting is not over. the taliban, now concentrated in the south of the country and on the pakistani border, will do everything in their power to try to save, at any cost, what power and ability to harm they have left. it would be a disaster if they succeeded in rallying the pashtun populations who felt rejected by the new masters of the country to their fatal plan. as for the various rival factions that make up the northern alliance, let us beware of idealizing them. the plight of women in some of the provinces she controls does not allow us to rest in peace. in addition, their past behaviour, which is only five years old, and the disturbing information coming from mazar-e-sharif unfortunately do not allow us to ignore the risk that sooner or later they will be involved in bloody settlements of accounts in the reconquered territories. experience shows that effective aids to military action can become serious obstacles months of drought and misery, and finally five weeks of intense bombing. in that devastated country, the un estimates that seven and a half million people are at risk of starvation. in this context, now be counted among the agents of change, and it is high time that we bring stability, dignity and peace to this martyred people.

- madam president, afghanistan is currently experiencing uncertain times which will prove crucial for the future. the end of the taliban's dictatorial rule opens the door to a democratic reconstruction which is still far from being won. an algerian-style islamist guerilla is likely, against which massive bombing is ineffective and which must be stopped. the european union must take strong and clear positions, because, as emma bonino and francis wurtz have said, afghan women must not be sacrificed in the process of political reconstruction. women's participation is the key to a sustainable reconstruction of afghanistan. they must be present at the first negotiations and be called upon to participate in a new government from the first day. this is the only solution that can guarantee the protection and respect of women's rights and all human rights. the european union cannot support a government project which does not take this essential aspect into account. the integration of women is also a first step towards democracy. unfortunately, this democracy cannot tolerate warlords who have been guilty of repeated violations of human rights, of multiple extortions and who care more about defending their ethnic group than the future of the country. we must put an end to the reign of impunity. the afghan people must be represented by a democratic, multiethnic, and human rights-respecting government.
- madam president, i welcome this debate today, at a time when the situation in afghanistan is changing from hour to hour and i hope in a positive way. i know that europe has two obligations towards afghanistan. we must, in conjunction with the un, play a part in the political settlement of the conflict, so that, as guy verhofstadt has said, a stable, legitimate, democratic government is established which is broadly representative of all ethnic groups and which respects the principles of human rights. but i think we have a second duty towards afghanistan, and that is a duty of urgency. we know that the humanitarian situation in afghanistan is tragic. the result of a combined effect of a war that has torn the country apart for 23 years and a drought that has been raging for three years. we know that 7 million people were already dependent on humanitarian aid before the military operations were launched. we also know that up to 100,000 children could die this winter if sufficient food does not reach them in the coming weeks. we therefore call for europe to take a major emergency action in response to this humanitarian tragedy. in the context of the consultation we want to continue between the european union, the united states, the neighbouring states of afghanistan, the un specialised agencies and the ngos working in afghanistan, we are calling - as you have done on several occasions, madam president - for the creation of secure humanitarian corridors to allow emergency food aid and shelter for the displaced afghans. this is not just an emergency, it is simply the duty of the people of the european union, whom we represent here.

- the agenda calls for statements by the council and the commission on the negotiations under the biological and toxic weapons convention following the recent anthrax attacks. i now give the floor to mrs durant, who will speak on behalf of the council.
the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to turn to the question of the negotiations on the biological and toxin weapons convention. the recent attacks of 11 september have only reinforced our conviction that multilateral disarmament and non-proliferation instruments are more essential than ever. every effort should be made to prevent terrorist organisations and their members from having access to more powerful means to carry out their criminal activities. the fight against biological weapons must therefore be pursued at an even faster pace, in particular in view of the threat of possible bioterrorist attacks. the convention on biological and toxin weapons is a fundamental instrument in this respect. the european union and its member states are committed to promoting its universality. the european union will, in view of the 5th review conference of the biological and toxin weapons convention, to be held in geneva from 19 november to 7 december 2001, make a fresh appeal to those states which have not yet acceded to the biological and toxin weapons convention to ratify it as soon as possible. the strengthening of the convention is also a priority for the union in the disarmament field. the council thus attaches paramount importance to the conclusion of the negotiations in geneva, within the ad hoc group, on a legally binding protocol establishing an effective regime for enforcing compliance with the biological and toxin weapons convention. in its conclusions of 11 june 2001, the council of the european union further confirmed its commitment to contribute to the drafting of a protocol containing a series of concrete measures which it had defined in its common position of 17 may 1999 as essential to the establishment of an effective instrument. in this regard, the union regrets that the task force has not succeeded in fulfilling its mandate, namely to conclude these negotiations on a legally binding protocol before the start of the 5th review conference. the union expressed its disappointment at the refusal of the united states to accept the synthesis text presented by the chairman of the working party. the council therefore maintains its position. the threat posed by biological weapons requires an appropriate multilateral response. the council will continue to stress the importance it attaches to the work leading to a legally binding instrument and, in particular, to the continuation of the task force. the union has taken note of the statement by the united states that it supports all currently existing multilateral mechanisms for arms export control, non-proliferation and verification, as well as its alternative proposals. the union is continuing its examination of these proposals. we have already discussed these with the united states and will continue to do so in the context of preparations for the review conference. the union reserves the right to make proposals as well. finally, the union hopes that the negotiating acquis will be preserved and that the review conference will be able to take decisions which offer prospects for a rapid resumption of negotiations in the multilateral framework of the convention, with the participation of all states parties.

- mr president, in this same house on 26 october 2000, i had already explained why bank charges for crossborder payments in europe, at their present level, are the result of technical obstacles which will hopefully disappear with time, but which are unavoidable for the time being. in these circumstances, the demonization of the euro by some is at once an obsession with the uniformity of the internal market and a blowback from the pro-euro propaganda which had promised impossible miracles. i have already dealt with these points and i will not go into them again. the proposal for a regulation under consideration today is the next step. since the market is resisting, it is proposed that force be used to force it to yield by decreeing the compulsory equality of bank commissions on domestic transfers as on cross-border transfers. we believe that this proposal is inappropriate not only because it ignores the realities of the market, which will take its revenge tomorrow in one way or another, but also for four reasons. firstly, it violates subsidiarity because this is a matter for the member states. secondly, it violates the freedom of prices, which we thought the commission was the vigilant guardian of, but for the euro, what great principles would we not accept to be sacrificed? thirdly, it violates the repeated commitments to use the wording of the regulation as little as possible, because by applying it directly to the territory of the member states, it circumvents the very legitimate power of transposition of the national parliaments. fourthly, it will lead to many more or less disguised forms of unfair treatment of citizens, since the real but forbidden costs of crossborder payments will have to be transferred to other banking products. that, mr president, is more than enough reason to reject this regulation.

in writing. - we voted against the proposal for a regulation on crossborder payments in euro, which seeks to force banks to not charge them by falsely claiming that they are free. this absurdity, motivated only by the desire to make it appear that the euro itself abolishes all these fees on cross-border payments, is likely to cost us dearly in all sorts of perverse effects. moreover, this proposal is legally flawed. it is based on article 95-1 tec, which concerns the establishment of the internal market. it should therefore apply in the same way to the 15 member states of the union. this is not the case, since three members of the union do not belong to the euro area. in these circumstances, it would probably have been more appropriate to give the regulation the legal basis of article 123-4 tec (last sentence) which concerns the measures to be taken for the introduction of the euro, and therefore applies only to the countries participating in the single currency. but article 123-4 requires unanimity in the council, and article 95 only a qualified majority. this is probably the factor that has been weighed in the balance, in order to overcome the reluctance of certain countries. the fact remains that it is difficult to imagine what the actual legal situation will be in non-euro area countries, which will be obliged to give a premium to cross-border transfers denominated in a currency which is not their own. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft regulation. of course, since the community has no competence in this area. the european parliament has tried to fill this gap by voting an amendment calling on the member states to define and adopt 'dissuasive' sanctions, but such an exhortation has no legal effect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs peijs' report and i would like to emphasize the quality of the work carried out by our rapporteur. i am glad that our assembly is finally taking a decision on such an important subject. clearly, the patience of european consumers has reached its limit. it is clear that the banks have gone too far in multiplying the unfulfilled promises, because they are sure that brussels will not dare to restrict the freedom of tariffs. the commission has been negotiating with them for eleven years... in vain. banks have always refused to make the necessary investments to make crossborder transfers cheap. this is particularly so since the present system allows them to make a considerable profit. the consumer is not the only one to bear these undue bank charges: smes working in exports suffer particularly, their competitiveness being burdened for no clear reason. the situation, which has been incomprehensible to smes and consumers since the introduction of the euro on 1 january 1999, is likely to become explosive with the changeover to the euro in cash in less than two months' time. how can we explain the fact that the euro area is a single payment area for banknotes and coins only, with all other means of payment being discouraged by strong banking punctions? how can we justify that a transfer from lille to bastia is cheaper than the same operation between lille and brussels? there is a concern that banks will use their tariff freedom to raise their domestic prices to make up for the shortfall in the euro area. however, as commissioner bolkestein said, "the banks know that public opinion has legitimate expectations". hopefully they do.
in writing. - in referring to europe's energy dependence, the report conceals the fact that the main dependence is less on other countries than on the big oil trusts which often also control other energy sources. it is this dependence that europe paid dearly for during the oil crisis in 1973, when these trusts decided to increase oil prices in general in order to make their least profitable deposits profitable. this dependence on trusts is reflected in the "serious risk of short-term price instability and long-term lack of resources", the report warns. it is not the unequal distribution of energy resources on the planet, a geological fact, that threatens the rational use of these resources in a way that respects the natural environment, but the fact that their management is carried out by large private groups, exclusively concerned with their profit rate, when they themselves do not suffer from the erratic fluctuations of the market, or even from stock market speculation. the problem goes beyond the european framework: the world's resources can only be rationally managed and shared out if a collective effort is made on a global scale, which implies an end to the domination of these resources by private groups and a completely different organization of the economy.
in writing. - i said in the plenary debate on tuesday evening that i supported the 'chichester package' on energy security, despite the demands for liberalisation of the energy sector which i could not have supported if they had been put forward in isolation but which, in this case, were part of a comprehensive, diverse and courageous 'package' which is advancing european thinking in this field. that's why i voted for the package. i still cannot understand how anyone can defend liberalisation which aims to bring down prices and which is expressed in the promotion of 'cheap' energy sources, and then complain about dependence on outside sources which increases as consumption increases (or does not decrease) because prices are very (or too) low! i hope to get a clear explanation on this point from the "founders" of liberalisation.
in writing. - the chichester report aims to present a 'european strategy' on the security of energy supply. but it is very difficult to see in the resolution even a single clearly stated guideline. anything can be said in it, and its opposite can be said as well. the real issues that underlie a "strategy" are avoided. can we restructure the energy sector without a real, sustained and concerted public policy? can we rely on the "market" (i.e. the private financial interests)? is energy a "common good" or just a commodity? how is the atomic risk acceptable ? the vows of piety are sprinkled with the resolution. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the renewal of the nuclear fleet, and that appropriate measures be taken to ensure the disposal of radioactive waste and the safety of the plants. that's asking the impossible. the chichester report is not only confusing but also in keeping with neoliberal policies. paragraph 18 wants to 'promote further market opening in the eu' and paragraph 42 considers that 'it is essential to complete the liberalisation of energy markets'. only a public service policy can meet social and environmental requirements and ensure 'sustainable development' in this sector of the economy. we vote against the resolution.
in writing. - the question of the energy supply of the member states is a fundamental element of their security which naturally falls primarily within the sphere of national sovereignty. however, given the important interactions of energy choices, it may be worthwhile, as the green paper does, to take a forward-looking approach and to study this issue at european level. this examination must, of course, be approached without any ideological prejudice which would demonize or romanticize any particular energy source. otherwise, we're leaving the rational discourse. this is the approach adopted in the chichester report, which, like the green paper, stresses the need for the member states to maintain a balanced mix of energy sources, thus giving full play to nuclear electricity. this is the only way to avoid making the european countries more dependent on the outside world. it is also the only way for the european union to meet its international commitments to limit co2 emissions into the atmosphere. research and development in nuclear energy must therefore continue in order to make the most of the scientific and industrial advances we have in this field, to ensure that our countries have maximum autonomy in energy resources, to preserve the environment and to achieve satisfactory disposal of final waste. i regret that the caudron report has not given full consideration to this last point, which is essential. if we do not do this, the increase in demand will inevitably be directed towards fossil fuels, which are both environmentally problematic and problematic in terms of security of supply.
in writing. - the report states in its preamble that water is "not a commodity like any other" and that "access to water is an inalienable human right". however, this claim is of little weight in the face of vivendi, suez and other large groups, which appropriate the "market" of water to extract juicy profits with the blessing of the states at their service. in fact, it sounds like a wishful thinking, considering the industries that pollute and squander the planet's resources for the greater good of their shareholders' bank accounts. in this 21st century, when the world has never had so many technical means, the social barbarity of capitalism is the main reason why a whole part of humanity does not have access to running water, or even to drinking water. the water problem, which is vital for hundreds of millions of people, extends far beyond the geographical boundaries of europe and, like many other problems, would require humanity to put an end to the dictatorship of the market, profit and competition. the rapporteur, drawing on this system, envisages the 'sustainable management of water resources' in terms of pricing and taxation. this means, once again, that those who can afford it, individuals and especially industrial groups, will be able to continue to waste and even pollute, while others, the poorer, will continue to be deprived of it. water, this vital resource, should be provided free of charge by society and its management should be planned according to actual needs and subject to democratic control by the population. the current profit-driven economic system is fundamentally incapable of ensuring 'sustainable management of water resources' and is thus a threat to the future of humanity in this and many other fields.
in writing. - shipbuilding has for years benefited from substantial subsidies from national governments and european institutions. this has not prevented it from reducing its workforce, even closing entire factories and throwing their workers out on the streets. the shipbuilding bosses are trying to get these subsidies to continue by invoking competition, but the money they would be paid would continue to increase the profit of these companies and be shared by their shareholders, even if the shareholders would release their capital as soon as the yards became less profitable and invest it elsewhere, without caring what happens to the workers. this is all the easier because many shipyards are dependent on industrial groups which, like alstom, have interests in several sectors and license in some of them while receiving subsidies in others. we have no intention of helping the shareholders of the large shipbuilding trusts in any way, and we have voted against this report. if shipbuilding is necessary for the european economy, it must be nationalised, not subsidised at the expense of its private owners.
in writing. - the schörling report has the merit of recalling that 'the european union is the world's leading producer of chemicals' and that 'it is high time (that) it developed (real) control of chemicals'; it is known that 'the vast majority of existing substances - on the market for at least 20 years! - have never been properly tested', and it is noted that some serious diseases are on the increase and that 'there seems to be a direct link (between) these diseases and exposure to chemical substances'. it therefore advocates strict control of chemicals on the market, testing of these products before they are put on the market - and the withdrawal of those which do not meet these tests - and a series of binding measures for manufacturers and commercial distributors to oblige them to ensure a minimum level of safety. this position takes account of the interests of the population but is not acceptable to the union of chemical industries, a french employers' organisation which, in a letter to meps, opposes the restrictions that would be imposed on companies producing or marketing chemical products. it is only this shameless lobbying by the chemical bosses that is motivating us to vote for the schörling report and the measures it proposes, even though the rapporteur is otherwise in favour of the market.
in writing. - i should like to state the reasons why i voted in favour of this report as amended. firstly, i think that this is a balanced approach which improves the protection of the environment and in writing. - the few sentences in the report on 'health, education and the fight against extreme poverty', 'the fight against drugs' or 'environmental protection', some of the objectives which the european union claims to defend in this region of the world, are only a facade of much less admirable intentions. by proposing as their 'ultimate objective' the 'bilateral and preferential, gradual and reciprocal liberalisation of trade in goods and services of all kinds between the two regions, in accordance with the rules of the wto', the countries of the european union are making a mockery of the fate of the peoples of latin america. first and foremost, they would like to catch up in penetrating the latin american markets, which are already badly affected by the presence of other, much more powerful predators, such as north american multinationals. instead of the promised development, the opening of markets to large corporations and financial institutions has plunged latin america into poverty. at least 224 million latin americans live in extreme poverty, that is more than 40% of the population of this region! and there is no question of cancelling the debts that are strangling these countries. we have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - to portray the airlines as having been affected by the september 11 attacks in the united states is a brazen lie. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. air france, for example, increased its dividend to shareholders by 22 percent just three days after the attacks in new york and washington. it has just bought air afrique and brought alitalia and the czech airline csa into its orbit. and, like other major european airlines, it has benefited greatly from the bankruptcies of aom-air liberté, sabena and swissair. this is the free play of the market, which national and european leaders claim should govern everything, the economy and the fate of workers. in recent years, it has caused the elimination of hundreds of thousands of jobs in europe in the airline sector alone, and this without the slightest stirring of national and european leaders, because the shareholders of the companies were pocketing huge profits, such as the very rich baron seillière, the french "boss of bosses". the 9/11 attacks were just a pretext for the airline capitalists to win new subsidies while continuing their offensive against their employees. and in this they have been aided and abetted by the various national governments. it has also been seen recently in france, belgium and switzerland, in the case of company bankruptcies, which have thrown tens of thousands of employees into the street, without any cost to the main protagonists and responsible for these bankruptcies, such as baron seillière. we therefore voted against this resolution which cynically invokes employment to cover new subsidies to the companies and capitalists in the airline industry, already responsible for hundreds of thousands of job losses.

commission. – madam president, i welcome the favourable reception that the commission proposal has received and i would like to thank parliament for its contributions aimed at further reinforcing the protection of workers affected by the insolvency of their employer. the insolvency directive has proved to be an invaluable instrument for protecting employees in cases of economic downturns and it will be a key legislative instrument to respond to the present climate of closures and redundancies. although the basic structure of the directive should be retained, specific points of the directive need to be revised. i welcome amendment no 2 which aims to prevent the introduction of new restrictions beyond those currently in place in the member states, and also amendment no 9 which proposes to prohibit threshold provisions in order to qualify for claims under the directive. i am also in favour of amendment no 4 which proposes to extend the protection of workers of employers in other insolvency situations beyond those situations covered by the definition of insolvency proposed by the commission. firstly, the broadening of the definition is fully acceptable. however, on amendment no 6, the extension to any other procedure or even to "de facto" situations of insolvency can only be accepted as an option for the member states and not as an obligation. i can also accept amendment no 11, which proposes to add severance pay on termination of the employment relationship, with the addition of the term "where appropriate". the term "pay" should continue to be defined in the national law of the member states. amendment no 14, which proposes the abolition of a ceiling, is not acceptable in its entirety but i share your concerns on this point and i could accept a provision which allows ceilings which are compatible with the social purpose of the directive in order to avoid a level which is unacceptable for workers. i am also ready to supplement this provision with a non-regression clause which impedes member states from lowering the protection already provided when implementing the amended directive. finally, i can accept the reintroduction of the old article 5 of the directive – amendment no 15 – but this only in the old unchanged version of this article in the 1980 directive. i am unable to accept the remaining amendments, in particular amendment no 13 which aims to increase the minimum period for pay to six months. such an increase would seriously reduce the chance of the directive being adopted and would place a further considerable financial burden on the public purse and employers which would in turn cast doubt on the system of pay guarantees as a whole. i cannot accept amendment no 1, which aims to prevent employees from being "converted" to self-employed persons; amendment no 7 which proposes the introduction of a community definition of "employee"; nor amendments nos 8 and 16 which propose to add categories of workers who may not be excluded from the scope of the directive. efforts to combat illegal "conversion" must be made at national level. a community definition of an employed person should not be included in a particular directive, and self-employed workers cannot be covered because they do not have an employer who could be insolvent. in line with your comments i agree that there are different types of self-employed people. there are some self-employed people who are economically dependent. this issue was raised in 2000 when we had consultation with the social partners. the responses of the social partners emphasised the need to clarify and analyse the situation in all member states because there is a diversity of situations, there are many different kinds of self-employed people. this was the reason why we have already launched a study which will provide us with an overview of the nature of the phenomenon across the european union. once we have the results of the study, the commission will analyse it and after a consultation with the social partners we will present the appropriate way to deal with this issue. the other categories – home-workers and those in similar categories – are covered to the extent that they are considered to be employees under national law. there is, therefore, no need to mention them specifically. finally, some amendments should be rejected because they would not help to achieve the underlying objective of the proposal. to sum up, i can accept, subject to some minor redrafting, amendments nos 2, 4, 6, 9, and 11, and parts of amendments nos 14 and 15. i reject amendments nos 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 16, 17 and 18. i would like to thank you for your contribution. i would particularly like to thank and congratulate mr bouwman for his contribution and for the report.

mr president, the very recent and all too frequent disasters in the mont blanc and gotthard tunnels are a dramatic indictment of the present transport policy in europe. and here, whistle blowing should be a conviction. the road transport sector seems to have been freed from any legal framework, any standard of control. freight companies are exempted from licensing, and work permits are becoming optional for drivers who are increasingly coming from outside the community, when their driving time is close to the norm and they are close to sleeping. how many more gothards and mont blancs have to go up in flames before they are covered by strict legislation and an effective, harmonized, european control system? the people of all sensitive or densely populated areas and all professions are calling for europe here, and there is a vital urgency. today, the sensible thing would be to arrange security escorts in every major tunnel for the convoys of trucks. until this first safeguard is put in place, there will always be the risk of life and death in reopening these two damaged tunnels. we must not wait any longer to see this harmonization of safety standards for tunnels, but we must clearly point the finger and denounce this political frivolity and the lack of commitment on the part of the public authorities to the necessary but costly redevelopment of the underground corridors. if road transport practices need to be reformed, a fundamental rethinking of our transport policy requires the same strength. the tragedies in the tunnels demonstrate the practical and ideological dead ends of the entire highway, which clogs some transportation routes, suffocating our entire environment. the commission has already taken the initiative in the field of transport, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support the amendments tabled by the committee on transport and tourism, which are aimed at improving the quality of transport services and the quality of the transport services provided by the various transport modes. the memory of the victims of the gotthard and mont blanc must stimulate in us a new spirit, more considerate and respectful of our modes of transport.

the commission. mr president, the dramatic consequences of the accident at saint-gothard, and indeed the tragic consequences of the mont blanc and thorain tunnels, make the question of tunnel safety all the more urgent. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the first is improved tunnel specifications and the second is the reinforcement of rail transport of road vehicles through the alps. the commission's white paper, to which almost all members referred, announced that it would propose european regulations setting minimum safety standards for tunnels. these standards concern technical equipment, traffic rules, user information, rules for the training of tunnel operators, accident personnel in case of problems and rescue services. it is a complex project that must take into account a multitude of different parameters if we consider the great differences that exist between the tunnels, both because of geographical features and because of dimensions and because of traffic density. the commission, with the help of eminent experts, is currently preparing a proposal for parliament early in 2002. the commission will also be inviting a meeting of political and economic actors from the alpine and pyrenean regions. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the introduction of a new system of national of course, this particular accident brings up again the question of the transport of goods in the alpine region. the commission's proposal for a directive on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to road transport is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done on this. the european commission has also financed studies between 1994 and 2000 to build the new lyon-turin rail link, which has so far cost 60 million, or 50% of the total. this project, for which the community is by far the largest single donor, is one of the 14 projects approved by the european council in essen in 1994 and which, unfortunately, will not be able to be implemented until 2010. the brenner railway should also be put into operation as soon as the railway transport potential of road vehicles in the alps should be exploited immediately. this accident, with its dramatic consequences, is another reason why every effort should be made to convert road freight transport to rail, a mode of transport which in europe accounts for only 8% of the market, while in the united states it has reached 40%. the european commission has also taken new initiatives. in january 2001, it proposed that the council sign, on behalf of the european commission, the protocol on transport annexed to the alpine convention, as a political message to restore equity between the different modes of transport. in view of the difficulties in financing these projects, the white paper proposes community legislation to establish fairer pricing principles to take possible to finance major railway infrastructure projects, thus applying the swiss system. the commission also intends to make any community financing of transeuropean networks conditional on the strictest safety standards being met. in conclusion, the commission has taken or is about to take a number of concrete measures to solve the specific problems of the pyrenees, the alps and other sensitive areas. i would like to assure you that every effort will be made to guarantee users the highest level of security.

commission. – mr president, i should like to thank the members of parliament for their kind remarks concerning echo and i shall convey these congratulations to mr nielson, the commissioner responsible. firstly, as far as hurricane michelle is concerned, the commission has been closely monitoring its effects in central america in the caribbean area since the beginning of the crisis, in cooperation with our experts and partners in this field. michelle started on 29 october as a tropical storm off the northern coast of nicaragua and honduras, where it caused severe floods. the communication systems proved their efficiency as they were the only working systems that allowed for a quick evaluation in areas of difficult access such as moskita. on 1 november, echo started discussions with the ngos present in the field to establish emergency systems, particularly in the moskita region in honduras and nicaragua – the areas worst hit. on 4 november, michelle became a hurricane that crossed cuba and touched jamaica. fortunately, the local authorities had undertaken timely evacuation measures. echo services decided on funding once an initial evaluation of the hurricane damage had been carried out in cuba. this decision to allocate eur 1 050 000, should be approved by the end of this week and will cover the moskita region in honduras and nicaragua, cuba and jamaica. the decision will mainly involve the evacuation of people in danger, food aid for honduras, the provision of temporary shelter in jamaica and the distribution of water, sanitation and health packages in all countries. members of this house have raised two main issues. one concerns nicaragua. i should like to assure you that all the distributed funds are regularly monitored and no position on cuba, announced on 25 june 2001. but it kept being said cuba had not been given any humanitarian aid until now. in fact cuba has benefited from around eur 125 million in aid since 1993, european union common position which i have already referred to. as far as algeria is concerned, the situation in the country is very complex. there are many different kinds of problems, but i will - doc. b5-0723/2001 by mr swoboda, on behalf of the group of the european people's party, on small arms; - b5-0729/2001 by mr morgantini and mr brie, on behalf of the gue/ngl group, on the control of international arms transfers and arms brokering; - b5-0730/2001 by mr maes, mr mckenna and mr schroedter, on behalf of the green group in the european parliament, on the control of international arms transfers and arms brokering.
- madam commissioner, mr president, like some hotbeds of conflict of small geographical and media size, certain categories of so-called light weapons are also of 'small legislative and financial size', that is to say, insufficiently covered by legislation and cheap. it is no wonder that weapons of this kind are the fuel for these forgotten conflicts. yet the sheer number of victims should alarm us, if there were no poverty to cover them up. however, an international consciousness has emerged, through the united nations programme of action, to contain and regulate the transfer, or should we say the trafficking, of these small arms and light weapons which are responsible for heavy human losses. the current international context, with the armed coalition in afghanistan and the international fight against terrorism, makes it even more necessary to join and support this voluntary and pioneering approach of the united nations. the europe of defence, of national staffs, cannot be the only military arm of the european union. it must be based on a europe of the prevention and control of the arms trade by means of a coercive legislative arsenal aimed at all levels of the industry. the arms dealings, export and detention authorizations, as well as extradition and police cooperation procedures must be the focus of our legislation and be the subject of a process of harmonization in our european union. instead of trying to intervene in conflicts that are flaring up, wouldn't it be better to defuse them in the first place? the legislative structure of the union today allows this to happen while its military aspect is still being prepared. europe must seize this opportunity.
the commission. mr president, the accumulation of small arms in many parts of the world is creating conditions of destabilisation and crisis, and the european union is committed, within its means, to combating this phenomenon. in the context of the joint action of the european union on small arms and light weapons, it is proposed to introduce a series of confidence-building measures, including measures to improve transparency. the union shall undertake to provide financial and technical assistance to states, international organisations and non-governmental organisations which request support for these purposes. the european union welcomes the results of the united nations conference on the illicit trade in small arms and admits, as has been said by the honourable members, that the results could have been more concrete, more clear. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we particularly welcome the decision to hold a new conference before 2006 to review and assess progress by that date.

- mr president, the draft declaration which the laeken council is to publish to organise the debate on the future of the union seems to us to have been prepared under very curious conditions. the belgian presidency's entourage is reportedly boasting that it deliberately did not give the text to its partners too soon so that they would not have time to rewrite it. this is not a very cooperative way of working and it is why we are warning the members of the council: remember that you represent countries, national democracies, which must keep their hands free in this negotiation. it would have been ideal to have set up, as a first step, an interparliamentary forum consisting of representatives of national parliaments or working on the basis of proposals from national parliaments, since the latter constitute a good level for summarizing the sentiments of each nation. in any case, ladies and gentlemen, heads of state and government, do not allow yourselves to be forced into a mechanism which would lead to proposals which are out of step with the interests and preferences of our peoples. this is a point which i shall elaborate on in my explanation of vote on the resolution which will be tabled.
- mr president, the question of european governance is a very complex problem, and one which our fellow citizens do not understand very well, which is a paradox. we are all aware that europe is suffering from a serious democratic deficit, and that is why there is obviously a need for a fundamental reform of the way in which power is exercised at european level. we must do so with three objectives in mind: to clarify the decision-making process, to improve its efficiency and transparency, and to encourage citizen participation. i therefore support the guidelines contained in the white paper and the kaufmann report. of course, we must ensure greater transparency in the work of the council, we must encourage greater participation of the european parliament and national parliaments in the legislative process, we must simplify community legislation and create the conditions for genuine consultation with civil society. in addition, as the committee on constitutional affairs has pointed out, i think it would be useful to draw up an interinstitutional agreement on co-legislation, which would guarantee the european parliament the effective exercise of its role and political responsibility. this governance reform is therefore moving in the right direction. but it will obviously never replace the fundamental reform we so vitally need in our institutions. we must quickly adopt a simple and legible constitution, clearly defining the distribution of powers, specifying the roles of each individual so that the citizen can finally understand who is doing what and who is responsible. finally, as we all know in this chamber, there is no democratic power without democratic legitimacy. that is why it will be necessary one day - and i hope as soon as possible - for the president of the european executive to be elected by universal suffrage.
- madam president, since we are talking about human rights, i should like to comment on a question of method, which applies to all association agreements. today there will be a joint debate on the association agreements with egypt, together with oral questions and motions for resolutions. in the interests of a democratic debate and a more consistent vote on all association agreements, it is important to have separate sessions. we suggest that the debate should first be on oral questions and resolutions and then on the vote on the association agreements. it is neither logical nor consistent to take a position at the same time. the oral questions and resolutions are intended to challenge the political authorities of these countries and to give them time to debate and respond. this two-step approach allows us to confirm the fundamental importance we attach to the whole agreement, in particular to article 2 on human rights. the example of egypt is a good example of how we do not ignore a decision which constitutes a violation of human rights - the final condemnation of homosexuals - and which flouts the values we defend in article 2 of our agreements. the group of the european people's party therefore wishes to keep the debate and vote on oral questions and motions for resolutions at one sitting and to postpone the association agreements to another sitting. we have already written to the president to ask for this.
- madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the fight against terrorism is an absolute necessity whose legitimacy cannot be questioned, at the risk of our democracies collapsing. but it must not be used as an excuse to muzzle our fundamental rights and democratic freedoms. how can we justify a european counter-terrorism proposal if no added value can be generated? the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. since public enemy number one is terrorism, why not limit the european arrest warrant to terrorist offences? if the illegal seizure of state or government facilities, public transport, infrastructure, public places, is a terrorist offence or if the legitimate exercise of our freedoms of expression, association, trade union rights, is tomorrow liable to be criminalised or labelled as terrorist, if these elements are retained, we will, by voting for these reports, renounce all our democratic rights. an explicit guarantee of these rights and freedoms must be included in this proposal for a framework directive. we are also concerned about certain offences that could fall within the scope of the mandate, since the criterion is the penalty, whereas the accused person deserves protection, like migrants and asylum seekers. even the support given to these people would become, tomorrow, guilty of terrorism. a minimum of harmonisation of the criminal procedures of the member states is necessary to ensure the principle of equality before the law, to guarantee the protection of rights in the principle of collegiality. in addition, since minors cannot be the subject of an arrest warrant, their criminal status must also be harmonised. the establishment of an area of security, freedom and justice requires that these three dimensions be fully effective. unfortunately, we see that the security aspect dominates the policy of the union and the member states. the fight against terrorism must be translated into security for all residents without any exclusion and full respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. finally, if a new text is to be adopted by the council tomorrow, we hope that our assembly will be consulted again.

mr president, i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the draft agreement with egypt. the draft agreement contains 92 articles which deal not only with economic and social aspects but also with political dialogue, a factor of progress and peace. it was negotiated for over seven years under difficult conditions. the consequences of such a postponement have certainly not been considered by the applicants, especially in the current international context. it should be remembered that unlike some other arab countries, egypt has never been a breeding ground for terrorists. on the contrary, egypt has paid a heavy price for terrorism. it would be irresponsible not to approve this agreement. it's unrealistic to try to match our models. imposing our own law is unrealistic. ignoring the culture, the identity, the sovereignty of egypt is unrealistic. this agreement must be endorsed by the member states and by us. we owe it to the union, because it will be one of the essential components of the necessary relaunch of the barcelona process. we also owe it to egypt, a great friend whose role in promoting peace in the middle east is well known.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, thank you for being here. i am pleased and honoured to have been appointed as rapporteur for the association agreement between the union, the member states and the arab republic of egypt, and i am aware of the importance of this agreement for both the union and egypt, as it seems to me to be balanced and fair to both parties. the arab republic of egypt is the most populous country in the arab world, with over 66 million inhabitants. egypt occupies a key geopolitical position and plays a leading role. egypt was the first arab country to establish diplomatic relations with israel. since then, the country has continued to play a moderating role in the region. relations between the european union and egypt are longstanding. the first cooperation agreement was signed in 1972. let us not forget that the union is egypt's main trading partner. egypt is also a major beneficiary of cooperation with the union: €686 million was paid under meda i between 1996 and 1999. the report we're interested in is about a new generation. the main objective of the project is to contribute to peace and security in the region and to stimulate trade and economic relations between egypt and the european union, as well as between egypt and its mediterranean partners. the draft agreement, which is based on respect for democratic principles and fundamental human rights, focuses in particular on the following main aspects: the establishment of a free trade area between the european community and egypt, leading to the abolition of duties on industrial products within 12 to 15 years of the entry into force of the agreement; regional cooperation, including through the establishment of a free trade area in the euro-mediterranean region; economic and financial cooperation in a wide range of areas, including the fight against terrorism; the european union and its member states will continue to work together to promote the development of the union's external relations. i am glad that this proposal was voted unanimously by the members of the committee on foreign affairs, which shows the interest it arouses. it also allowed for a number of concerns or fears to be expressed, some of which were justified, others less so. let me take two of them. the problem of the coptic minority, first of all. coptic christians make up more than 10 percent of the population. clearly, while not systematically oppressed, they do not enjoy the same rights and duties as their fellow muslims. on the other hand, it is clear that some of the problems are caused by extremists who are doing everything they can to stir up tensions between the two religious denominations. however, progress has been made, as confirmed by the coptic religious hierarchy, with the recent construction of monasteries and churches, despite the administrative hassles imposed by the texts. second, the court cases that have gone down in history, including the egyptian one, involved individuals or groups. we have to move beyond initial judgments. the judges of the first instance are sometimes sensitive to fundamentalist views and condemn harshly. but sometimes the high court overturns these initial judgments and applies a more lenient law, in accordance with democratic principles. i am aware that progress still needs to be made in the area of equity and justice, but it is clear that steps have been taken. the opposition and ngo officials i met there confirmed these advances. in general, the draft report has raised some questions. i share some of them, but i cannot vouch for those of us who are very willing to become teachers, singers of human rights, and who do not sweep up their own house. the egyptians are very good and right to remind us of our own imperfections, our laxity in many areas, including the fight against terrorism. we are reminded that our member states are a haven for terrorists and murderers, including egyptians, who live and act there with impunity. let 's be careful ! most egyptians, and not a few, are not willing to support this agreement. they insist that it gives too much to the european union, especially in the economic field, and that it will allow interference in the internal affairs of the state at any time. the recent letter from the people's assembly is untimely but significant in this respect. in these circumstances, i hope that parliament will vote by a large majority in favour of ratifying this agreement. may it strengthen the role of the european union in this part of the world and contribute to peace.
