- madam president, commissioner, in doha the fourth wto ministerial conference was to set an agenda and a programme. it has been done and, from that point of view, it is a success. but a success for whom? i am sure that you have succeeded, commissioner, in proving your nighttime endurance and your excellent health. as regards health, doha was a real success in terms of medicines, but it was osama bin laden who gave the world's poor the right to medicines. if the united states had not been afraid of the coal disease and had not had to confront bayer's intellectual property, they would not have given in. apart from that, what has doha brought us? two things: clichés and a reprieve. the clichés are piling up. first, the clichés about global trade that will bring growth, prosperity, stability and of course peace. we had already signed a trade agreement in marrakesh and everyone knows that it brought peace to gaza, palestine and even peace in afghanistan. second big cliché, europe would have held out, but japan gave up. the ldcs, despite the gift of everything but weapons, have abandoned it. maybe korea is staying. the union of the fifteen has been split. agricultural france was left alone, apart from the support of ireland. however, europe has won a victory over the environment and the social. on the environment, the united states, which is not a party to kyoto, is not bound; the european union has a long history of supporting the development of the social dimension. europe also got a reprieve. first, a reprieve from farming. until the end of the negotiations, and therefore until 2005, our farmers will receive internal aid and refunds. after that, we agreed to delete them. but the french jacques chirac and lionel jospin demanded a postponement to pass the presidential election quietly. they have obtained a reprieve, a reprieve in the execution of the death sentence of the cap, so much so that when polish farmers join europe, they will be deceived because they are joining the europe of the cap and there will be no more cap after 2005. we also got a moratorium on foreign investment. the ami had been thrown out of the oecd window and returned through the wto door. we also got a stay on our pensions. insurance companies will not be able to take over this large market right away. doha report: the european agricultural model is broken, the european cultural exception is forgotten, the european social model is in danger in the long term. what will be left of europe? a vast free trade area and everyone knows, since adam smith, that free trade is the misery of nations.
- doha was supposed to be the development cycle. but what did the developing countries gain from doha? i do not share the optimism of my colleagues on this point. so the agreement on access to medicines, which appeared to be a victory, is actually a sham that has deceived the media and developing countries. the clarification of the trips agreement, which is presented as a major issue at this conference and as a major concession to the developing countries, and the interpretation we have always given it, is certainly a political victory, but it does not change anything in the legal sense: it has no value before the wto dispute settlement body and the question remains open, as mrs kinnock has reminded us, for countries which do not have production capacity. at the moment, there is nothing to enable them to use compulsory licences to have others manufacture the medicines they need, as was also stressed at the recent ouagadougou conference. similarly, the wto's last-minute waiver and reciprocity rule for eight years for the signatory countries of the cotonou agreement appeared to be a given. in fact, this authorization, which the acp countries have been waiting for for months, is tantamount to blackmail against them. they had to sign the final declaration in doha, otherwise their request would be rejected. these are therefore minimal gains, which have served as a bargaining chip for western allies in favor of launching a new cycle. in reality, what happened in doha has often been a cynical play: we are increasingly engaged in a path of unbridled liberalism and, as we keep saying, a thorough reform of the wto is really necessary.

- commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, as a member of the parliament's delegation to doha, i too would like to welcome the excellent work of our commissioners and the results achieved, which have undoubtedly been very positive and which testify to the great efficiency of our commissioners in this negotiation. i also want to welcome, and above all, the excellent cohesion and solidarity between our three european institutions present in qatar. on the substance, and confining myself to the agricultural issue, i note with interest that the european union retains the necessary margin of manoeuvre for reforming its common agricultural policy in response to the new expectations of our society, since non-trade considerations are explicitly mentioned in the final ministerial declaration. this seems to me to be the key element in the outcome of doha. the priority for european agriculture today must no longer be export competitiveness at any cost, but the satisfaction of social demand in terms of food security, rural development and sustainability. the union can also count on its success vis-à-vis the united states, since all forms of export aid will be subject to the negotiation of the new round. finally, it seems to me that the union can welcome the strengthening of special and differential treatment for the developing countries. it should enable them to meet their needs, including food security and rural development. this in turn is more favourable to the growth of food-producing agriculture; it is therefore very important in the context of the world food demand, which is expected to double in the next 25 years as a result of the population growth of the developing countries and the improvement in the living standards of the emerging countries. overall, i think this agreement strikes a good balance between trade liberalization and regulation and also between trade and the development of all agriculture. i simply hope that the hopes thus aroused will be confirmed in the negotiations for the new round.

priority: we already have comparable data from other countries. the community added value should be expressed upstream in the form of a reduction in health risks arising largely from our environment in the broad sense: transport, pollution, chemicals, food, etc., but also from our behaviour and social, economic and environmental inequalities. we are advocating prevention throughout the world, but - ladies and gentlemen, the conclusions of the tampere summit have given a new impetus to the achievement of an area of freedom, security and justice. to achieve the objectives set, an action plan has been drawn up, which provides for a timeframe of two to five years after the entry into force of the treaty of amsterdam. at mid-term, the state of play of the tampere agenda should be assessed, taking into account the commission's scoreboard. the area of security, freedom and justice has three main dimensions: a community policy on asylum and immigration, strengthening judicial cooperation and police cooperation. what can we say about each of these three areas? as regards asylum and immigration policy and, more specifically, the management of migration flows, the measures taken conceive of immigration as a labour palliative and compensation for the demographic imbalances of states, without taking into account the human and social dimension or the consequences of brain drain. however, is not the universality of fundamental rights being called into question in the context of this community migration policy? is the readmission policy in line with international commitments on refugee protection and asylum? as for the european observatory on migration, let me express a reservation about it. it is true that some preliminary thinking is required as to the mission, usefulness and place of migrant ngos in this new structure. no significant steps have been taken to ensure fair treatment of third-country nationals. the question of their political participation and the redefinition of citizenship is being avoided under the pretext of preserving national sovereignty, which amounts to denying the democratic rights of citizens living in europe. how does the commission intend to promote citizenship of residence as a link to the law? and what action does the council intend to take on the directives on family reunification, the european status of longterm non-european residents, and freedom of movement, residence and work in the territory of the member states? the geneva convention forms the basis of asylum policy. however, the concept of refugee must include both the gender and the social dimension. is the council prepared to take account of the specific sufferings of women or victims of civil wars? does the eurodac system, based on fingerprinting, not pose a risk to the rights of asylum seekers? and should the dublin convention not be revised? the determination of the competence of the state to examine the case and the responsibility for the decision should depend on the choice made by the asylum seeker as to the state of residence and not the country of arrival, which is so difficult to define in our area which is supposed to be without frontiers. the action plans adopted for partnership with third countries are increasingly resembling a crackdown on immigration. what about development aid, the corollary of the curb on emigration? is cooperation limited to financing the expulsions? is the administrative police stationed at the border crossing points in third countries not a denial of the right to seek asylum? progress has been made at civil level in strengthening judicial cooperation. several texts were adopted on jurisdiction, the service of documents and the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions and their enforcement, particularly in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility. a proposal for a directive on legal aid is under consideration; it aims to ensure better access to justice. the balance sheet, on the other hand, is much more mixed on the strengthening of judicial cooperation in criminal matters: reluctance is expressed in particular on the classification of offences. at the legislative level, the protection of the euro against counterfeiting, money laundering, human trafficking and the sexual exploitation of children have resulted in framework decisions. it seems that the council is also preparing to adopt those of these decisions which concern the fight against terrorism and the european arrest warrant. the slow progress achieved is mainly due to the resistance of the member states to the principle of mutual recognition. the establishment of eurojust is a real step forward for citizens; the rights of the persons concerned and the protection of data must, however, be better guaranteed. unfortunately, we find that we are still a long way from a european prosecutor's office and common legislation and judicial procedures. the most significant progress has been made in the area of police cooperation. they are characterized by a multiplication of instances for which coordination is necessary. the terms of europol's participation in joint investigations, the feeding of its files and cooperation with third countries must be clearly defined. is it not urgent to guarantee better data protection and finally to ensure democratic and judicial control? in view of the respect for fundamental rights, should the list of safe countries not be revised? as for the schengen information system, with the prospect of enlargement of the union, new questions arise as to its functions, technical capabilities and institutional form. the 'justice and home affairs' programme has an external dimension which must not be overlooked. the fight against trafficking in human beings and the fight against organised crime are both areas which should be dealt with in the jha's external relations. in writing. - for more than 30 years, europe has chosen to build an original model of partnership with the countries of africa, the caribbean and the pacific. it is in the context of this approach of openness and solidarity that the common organization of the banana market was set up to guarantee access to the european market for some of the products of these acp countries, some of which are among the poorest in the world. this system has been opposed since its inception by the large multinational companies in the banana sector, whose production is very competitive, but often at the cost of exploitation that is close to slavery! from political pressure in the form of economic sanctions and compromise in the form of concessions, the whole system of quantitative protection must be dismantled as from 2006 in favour of a system of protection based solely on tariffs, the effectiveness of which is currently unknown in safeguarding the interests of traditional acp banana producers. the trade war that has poisoned transatlantic relations for nearly a decade has been brought to an end by the compromise reached in april 2001. but some of its provisions are a real 'bitter potion' for the acp countries: the end of the quota protection which guaranteed access to the european market for its traditional producers in 2006, a reduction of 100 000 tonnes in the guaranteed production quantity since january 2002, and the malfunctioning and delays of the technical and financial assistance system which was supposed to help acp producers adapt to new market conditions, but whose payments are still delayed. the report by michel dary on which we are debating today proposes that during the transitional period before the unknown of the end of the wto bananas, several 'safety nets' be granted to the acp countries. in writing. - since 1993, the banana issue has been at the heart of trade relations between the european union and the united states. some even say that it is poisoning transatlantic relations and that this conflict should be ended as soon as possible. i want to say at any cost. from louis vuitton to hermes to gucci, the powerful of this world have had enough! it is enough that from the west indies to brussels and strasbourg, some have chosen resistance rather than renunciation. but who in this parliament can ignore that by giving in to the dictates of the united states under the guise of the wto, the european union is guaranteeing the more or less long-term unemployment of 35 000 canarians or 30 000 west indians? who can fail to see that by giving in on this issue europe is turning its back on its social model, which it is constantly trying to export throughout the world? finally, who can fail to realize that by giving up on this issue today, we will give up on sugar tomorrow (not just cane sugar but also beet) and that soon we will have to decide to abandon our agricultural model? mr dary has not avoided these various questions, and i think that our assembly can take the honour of voting on his report today. we have chosen to resist the european commission's intransigence, because we are convinced of our democratic legitimacy. our request for 'cyclone' licences when production is destroyed, and especially our request to refuse the automatic transition to a purely tariff regime in 2006, are the most perfect illustration of this. that is why i naturally voted for the report by our colleague, which i consider to be generally relevant, despite the reservations i expressed to him about the distribution within the c quota between caribbean and african producers. in fact, given the african trade routes, which have historically been directed towards france, i fear that this amendment will be another blow to the european producers of guadeloupe and martinique.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to recall the history of this report, which was initially entrusted to the parliamentary committee on industry, like the other reports in the telecoms package. i was appointed rapporteur until the legal affairs committee declared itself competent on the merits and entrusted the report to malcolm harbour, a british member of the epp. i remained rapporteur for opinions, opinions which did not carry much weight in the discussions! it is a pity, especially when it comes to defending universal service in such an important and progressive field. the report adopted by the legal affairs committee last november is surprisingly light on the universal service provisions and focuses mainly on consumer protection. as i said in my report for an opinion, while the definition of universal service includes criteria of the same kind as those generally used for the evaluation of services provided to consumers (affordability, availability, delivery time, quality), its raison d'être is governed by objectives of a different nature in the field of regional policy, social policy (avoiding the exclusion of the less favoured) or public security policy. i would also like to stress the democratic challenge of access to the new communication networks. the new technologies offer citizens the opportunity to have a say, to participate in democratic debate and to influence decisions. they are also a valuable means of rebuilding the relationship. local democratization has much to gain from the interactivity of local public services online. it is through these new technologies that public services can be given a new lease of life if we have the means and, of course, the will. finally, access to the internet is essential for the creation of the knowledge-based information society. to meet these challenges, therefore, the committee's proposal had to be improved, which i tried to do in my amendments, which were rejected in their entirety by mr harbour. we have therefore voted today on a report which proposes interesting amendments concerning the protection of consumers - particularly disabled consumers - and the 'must carry' but which, i regret, cannot claim to set the framework for the universal service in this area!

- the common position (a5-0440/2001) by mr watts, on behalf of parliament's delegation to the conciliation committee, on the joint text approved by the conciliation committee for a european parliament and council directive amending council directive 95/21/ec on the application to ships calling at community ports or in waters under the jurisdiction of member states of international standards for ship safety, pollution prevention and shipboard living and working conditions (port state control) (pe-scon 3657/2001 - c5-0525/2001 - 2000/0065 (cod)) - the report (a5-0441/2001) by mr ortuondo larrea, on behalf of parliament's delegation to the conciliation committee, on the joint text approved by the conciliation committee for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending council directive 94/57/ec laying down common rules and standards for ship inspection and survey organisations and for the relevant activities of maritime administrations (pe-cons 3656/2001 - c5-0526/2001 - 2000/0066 (cod)); - recommendation for second reading (a5-0344/2001) on behalf of the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, on the common position of the council with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the accelerated introduction of double hull requirements or equivalent design standards for single hull oil tankers and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2978/94 (10221/1/2001 - c5-0389/2001 - 2000/0067 (cod)) (rapporteur: mr hatzidakis)
- mr president, a coincidence of timing means that today we are sadly commemorating the second anniversary of the sinking of the oil tanker erika. on 12 december 1999, on a stormy night, this oil tanker flying the maltese flag, certified by an italian company, with an indian crew, insured by a company based in bermuda, financed by a scottish bank, chartered by a shell company which sub-chartered it to an exotic subsidiary of the total group, carrying extremely polluting hydrocarbons belonging to another subsidiary of total, was sinking off the french coast, polluting 400 km of coast and causing considerable damage estimated at more than five billion francs. two years after that tragedy, where are we? the compensation of victims is falling. of the chf 5.5 billion in damages, the fipol scheme will cover only chf 1.2 billion, and the procedures are long, cumbersome and ineffective. the rest will be borne by the victims, the local authorities and the french state, under the application, not of the polluter-pays principle, but of the perverse principle of the victim-pays principle. the various measures we are discussing in the three reports by mr watts, mr ortuondo larrea and mr hatzidakis have been delayed too long. yes, we need to strengthen port state controls, mr watts; yes, we must make the work of classification societies more efficient, more reliable and more transparent, mr ortuondo larrea; yes, we must take concerted international action to eliminate single-hull tankers, but we must also be aware that double-hulls are no guarantee against shipwreck and stranding, mr hatzidakis. but why did it take more than two years after the disaster to take such basic measures in these three areas? and above all, two fundamental questions remain unanswered today, and it is not certain that the european level is the appropriate level for taking the appropriate decisions. the first is the question of compensation. compensation for the victims can only be complete. but today we are faced with a major disagreement at european level. some are in favour of a specific european fund, while others prefer an increase in the level of fipol. the disagreement persists, the case is blocked, while the united states, on the other hand, has unilaterally built a very efficient system of total compensation for which the consumer of the oil product is, in the final analysis, the financier, which is perfectly logical and legitimate. in europe, the member states are very unequal in the risks of marine pollution, and it would therefore be perfectly legitimate for the countries which are in the forefront in this respect to take the necessary initiatives themselves. i invite them to do so. the second fundamental question, which is still unresolved, is that of responsibility. we cannot allow cases like the erika to recur, where from a shell company in a tax haven, from a flag of complacency in a sub-charter, from a subcontractor in an offshore subsidiary, no less than eleven different companies were involved in the ship and its cargo, constituting a veritable labyrinth in which the real decision-makers, the real managers, can hide. this is a particularly unhealthy situation. it is necessary, at the level of the states most concerned and at the global level, to work urgently to ensure this clarification, this transparency in terms of responsibility, because, mr president, only the threat of very heavy and very severe sanctions will be able to deter the potential polluters of tomorrow.
- mr president, commissioner, on the anniversary of the sinking of the erika on 12 december 1999, our group and i are pleased to see the conciliation on three sets of proposals come to fruition. as regards the watts report, we are particularly pleased that the european parliament delegation has succeeded in making black boxes compulsory, which was not the easiest thing to do. this means that from now on the vessel will be immobilized unless it is equipped with a working vdr system. as regards the report by my colleague mr ortuondo larrea, the question of conflict of interest is in particular settled so that classification societies can no longer have any links with shipbuilders, owners, ship owners or charterers. the same applies to the question of the limits of the financial liability of these companies in relation to the financial balances of the recognised organisations. and there is also the problem, which mr souchet mentioned, of compensation by fipol or by a european fund, which must be ensured more effectively. it is also urgent to put an end, as mr hatzidakis said at the third reading, to the problem of single-hull boats, mainly with regard to the deadline of 2015, because maritime safety issues cannot wait any longer, now that two years have already passed since the sinking of the erika. intermittent pollution and garbage ships, such as the one that was recently said to have sunk off brest, are still too much of a news story, and the union's credibility is at stake to put an end to this situation.

sakharov prize laureate. – madam president, distinguished members of the european parliament, ladies and gentlemen, dear friends: it is with great emotion and excitement i receive this recognition today. this prize is an act of faith in the ability of the world to promote a sustained dialogue of tolerance and understanding. it only made my commitment towards a nobler future for the conflict in our region stronger and more persistent than ever. there are so many events that i would like to tell you about here, but the time i am given is limited. from my prison, for almost three years i wrote a book called 'letters underway' where i asked myself during the bleakest moment the following question: could it be possible for me to address in my book an israeli figure who is an artist, a father, a real human soul, a man or a woman who would abolish the image of a soldier guarding my solitary cell? when the answer was yes, i proceeded with my writing. as soon as i was out of prison, i took part in a writers' meeting in oslo where a few intellectuals from both sides met to discuss how they could contribute to peace. during ten days of ebbs and flows, the israelis talked much about the historic distress that befell the jewish nation and people. the palestinians talked about their daily suffering under occupation. but finally, after ten days, we were able to understand each other's needs. i could not forget one comment by an israeli writer. during this meeting, on the tenth day, he said, 'i always thought that man is evil... now i am not sure'. in that same year, 1993, my son fell dead to the bullets of the soldiers in his school. the event changed the taste of everything in my life, but i knew that a good human being is a living one. suffering, if we so decide, can be used as a power to heal rather than a blind struggle for revenge and hatred. the principle of an eye for an eye, makes the whole world blind. i knew how to use understatement as a means of compromise in my literature. it is true, however, that the conflict of man with his heart is the noblest sort of struggle. it is a pity that the conflict of today is between nations and cultures. left to the generals of war and enmity, they will make it a bloody history of terror. left to them, we will accept it for a fact that our world is either bad or mad. but those who have read history in a tolerant way, understand that what is needed is a mutual moral commitment towards the facts of existence and the human obligation towards life as the only valuable gift. abnormalities of all kinds do not have a race, or a religion, or a certain home. only civilisation has its own religion and faith and home. that is because there has been no unique civilisation as a creation of its own: all through history civilisations borrowed from each other and excelled most when they were able to share their merits and values. however, the recent fear of a clash between cultures is not groundless. there is an amazing imbalance between the rich and the poor, and there are a great deal of injustices that threaten the very principle of tolerance in our globe. yet, our insistence on dialogue between cultures is at its highest now, because we have to search into the roots of terror. as a writer living in an exceptionally troubled area, i must look at this issue of intercultural discourse as a story of attraction and excitement. whatever happens in our region is doomed to affect the whole world. that is not because we are the centre of the world. it is only because the spiritual roots sprang from recent appeal for humanitarian aid by the united nations. causes: there are several causes of the war in angola. looking at the patron who brought us here to strasbourg on 12 december, halfway between the 10th, the day of the declaration of human rights, and the 14th, the day of his death, i see that i could focus on one of the causes: intolerance. it is no accident that the un declared 1995 to be the united nations year for tolerance. we still have in our ears and in our minds the words of pope john paul ii's message on the world day of peace that same year, and those of dr. frederico mayor concertation and reconciliation. violence, never again! "talking about tolerance in my country has been very difficult because the roots of intolerance are deep because they are anchored in the political bipolarisation between the two most voted parties: mpla and unita. in this climate, talk of tolerance is seen either as a betrayal of these most voted parties - and ironically belligerent - or as a backward reaction if it comes from an independent person. in this climate, to speak of change would mean alternating power with the rival; but for us, as church and civil society, the shift for now would be to accept tolerance as a matter of survival, which therefore imposes itself from the grassroots to the top, from political parties to government, from civil society and the churches themselves to the national project. tolerance is the key word, as locke tells us, if we are to find an inclusive human basis for conflict resolution, including our own, towards harmonious development. in the angolan case, tolerance would be embodied in the peculiar aspect of national reconciliation, the foundations of which can only be found in permanent and comprehensive dialogue capable of breaking this permanent cycle of war. tolerance implies solidarity and fraternity, and the lesson we have learned from this europe is the lesson that emerges from this great assembly, here and now. human brotherhood, infiltrating all facets of our relationship, also draws attention to the economic side and its misconceptions. in this "sun" in which we are inserted, riches are both generators of wars and signs of solidarity. speaking specifically of extractive exploitation, i would say that it is high time to increase the transparency that would make it difficult to finance conflicts, but would also encourage the implementation of social investments ... in writing. - in this last plenary session of the european parliament for the year 2001, which is also the last before the introduction of euro coins and banknotes, it must be noted that the european parliament did not hold any solemn sitting, or even any debate, to welcome what, for all the federalist majority here, is in principle the greatest undertaking of european 'integration'. why is there silence, which has lasted for several sessions, disturbed only by pro-sovereignty voices? the answer is simple: the final stage of the single currency - the physical exchange of coins and notes from 1 january 2002 - is based on two huge frauds. firstly, it is completely useless from a technical point of view and serves only to satisfy the extremism of certain federalists who are absolutely in favour of uniform monetary signs throughout europe. in reality, we could very well have stayed in the present situation: one euro for international use, superimposed on national currencies. so we are going to upset people's habits, make their lives more difficult in the months ahead, probably further diminish their trust in their national institutions, and all of this for no real use other than the satisfaction of federalist passions. the second is that public opinion has never been properly informed, and has even been manipulated. at the time of maastricht, as in the years that followed, it did not fully understand the scope of the treaty, namely the disappearance of the franc. subsequently, every effort was made to make it appear that she was in favour of the project, which was not the case. today, awareness is brutal: 52% of the french think that the single currency has more disadvantages than advantages, compared with 33% who think the opposite (le figaro, 11 december); 62% would like to continue using the franc, compared with 32% who think the opposite (wall street journal, 11 december). the same percentage is found at european level. the deception is so widespread that next year, when the eyes are opened, we will not only have to review the euro, but also think about serious reforms of the european institutions so that such manipulations do not happen again.
in writing. - the vote which has just been taken is a further and exemplary illustration of the often hemiplegic behaviour of the european parliament. how can our assembly, with a large majority, adopt a proposal in which it expresses its 'firm resolve to fight terrorism jointly' with the united states and at the same time refuse to ask the palestinian authority to condemn terrorism with a large majority? i am astonished that almost 320 members voted against amendment no 6, which proposed what seems obvious, namely that our support for the palestinian authority and its institutions must go hand in hand with a firm condemnation of violence by the palestinian authority and the implementation of effective measures to stop terrorist attacks. what is the use of such a double language? by abandoning a policy of balance, we undermine our diplomatic credibility and cultivate a partisan image. do we want the next european mission to be sent to israel, as the one led by the belgian presidency was? why send such a mixed message to terrorists, as if there were good and bad terrorists? our condemnation of terrorism must be global and not tolerate any exceptions. we will be more comfortable in affirming our wish for the palestinian people to have a full state with all its attributes, fully sovereign. every people aspires to a real state, an expression of its sovereignty, and the palestinian people have the same right to it as any other people. but we are not helping the palestinian authority leadership to behave with the responsibility that belongs to state authorities by indulging in terrorism.
in writing. - the report by my colleague, mr fernando pérez royo, on financial guarantee contracts is important for the harmonization of the legal regime for financial instruments in europe. like my colleague, i am very much in favour of harmonizing these markets within a reasonable time. mr pérez royo's work is in that direction. the report is in line with my view of the future of european financial markets, but the french socialists have not followed the rapporteur on three points. article 2 (4) extends the scope of the directive to all economic operators and accordingly modifies the order of preferential creditors in cases of bankruptcy affecting the chances of recovery of undertakings by transferring to the creditor banks the ownership of assets which would thus escape preferential creditors (employees, social security and tax bodies). article 6 provides for the use by the beneficiary of the guarantee of financial instruments given under the pledge system, which poses difficulties in relation to property rights and the traceability of securities and thus jeopardises the transparency of european financial markets. finally, article 10 (2), as amended by amendment no 17, deletes the precise criteria for location, thus condemning any credible attempt to make our financial markets transparent and anticipating the work of the hague convention on private international law. the vote in plenary confirming the rapporteur's choice to extend the scope of the directive led the french socialists to vote against the whole text.

mr president, the question of the future of beekeeping in europe is at stake today. it is nothing less than saving a production chain. there is an urgency because, while our consumption of honey is increasing, our production is dangerously decreasing. our consumption is now more than twice as much as our production. and if our production is declining, it's mainly because of the devastating effect - now scientifically proven - of a number of systemic insecticides used to treat the seeds of large crops on the bee colonies, which are really decimated. this is not a one-off or special situation, but affects almost all european beekeepers today. in view of this situation, the commission's proposal, which is extremely weak, merely provides for statistical work and some promotional measures in connection with the renewal of the regulation. these proposals are clearly not up to the problems facing the sector. no one denies the need to refine the statistics, but this work must not take the place of the most urgent task: the rebuilding of the herds so that our beekeepers can save european honey production. promoting a product is a great thing, provided you have the product. we must also be particularly vigilant in the promotion of products in which we are very heavily in deficit, such as honey. the link between product and terroir must be promoted. i do not think that the european union is going to finance the promotion of chinese honey or argentinian or mexican honey: honey which has no guarantee of traceability, which has no quality control, which does not meet our standards and which is often nothing but flavoured glucose syrups. we cannot claim to want to promote the development of a more environmentally friendly agriculture in europe and let our beekeepers, who are not a powerful lobby, sink into indifference. they deserve our attention. all products, including honey, can be bought from abroad, but the pollination of our plants cannot be imported. we are in a crucial area for the preservation of our environment, of our biodiversity. i therefore welcome the work done by our excellent rapporteur, astrid lulling, and by the whole committee on agriculture, which unanimously adopted the amendments we tabled together. these open the way to the possibility of community funding to help european beekeepers to replenish their hives in response to the emergency; that's our number 10 point. the veterinary costs of beekeeping should also be treated as for other animals; that's our number five point. and to safeguard the future of our production in the long term, it is essential that the authorisation of plant protection products in the future take into account their effects on bees in terms of behavioural alteration and mortality; this is our 17th point. the precautionary principle must be applied here in a fundamental way. the commission must wake up, mr commissioner. the council must wake up. we have an emergency ! we in the house are sounding the alarm today! the european union would bear a heavy responsibility if it encouraged the disappearance of our beekeepers. i hope that all members will follow the wise, necessary and urgent unanimous proposals of our committee on agriculture.

commission. – mr president, the commission too is deeply concerned by the repetition of such a dramatic event. everyone has in mind the tragic deaths of 58 chinese stowaways in dover last year, but unfortunate people die almost every week trying to reach what they consider to be a unique area of peace and prosperity. smuggling and trafficking of human beings are nowadays increasingly carried out by criminal organisations which profit from the distress of women, men and children in search of a better life or in need of international protection. although many measures have already been taken at national level and under schengen cooperation to tackle this horrendous form of crime, the commission can understand the frustration expressed by parliament when confronted with the apparent failure of existing instruments. there is definitely a need for enhanced action and cooperation at national, european and international level. this is why the commission put forward in november a communication on a common policy on illegal immigration, aiming at creating synergy of national efforts by adding a european dimension. one of the main messages flowing from this communication is that preventing and fighting illegal immigration is part and parcel of a comprehensive migration policy. it is crucial in building up support for a common asylum regime based on the highest humanitarian standards, as well as genuine immigration policy in line with our tradition of hospitality and solidarity. more efficient controls at the external borders, improved consular cooperation and reinforced police and judicial cooperation, are key elements. nevertheless, there is more to it than that: partnership with countries of origin and transit, a policy of sustainable return for illegal immigrants and the fight against undeclared work are all essential in this regard. all this must be achieved in full compliance with international obligations and human rights. the framework decision on combating trafficking in human beings, the directive on carriers' liability and the directive and the framework decision on the liability of smugglers, already approved by the council, are only first steps. in a broader framework, it is crucial to ensure a swift ratification and a coordinated implementation of the un palermo convention against transnational organised crime and its two protocols on trafficking and smuggling, which now form the basis for a global recognition of the problem and a stronger approach to tackle it. the laeken summit is now only a couple of days away. this will be the occasion for a mid-term review of the implementation of the tampere conclusions. this should provide a unique opportunity to give a new impetus to a much needed common immigration and asylum policy. the union is indeed behind schedule in these areas. a major political effort to fill these gaps as soon as possible would be our best tribute to the memory of the victims of wexford. but rather than looking at the global perspective, the rich world has some soul-searching and wallet-searching to do. the general level of development assistance flowing from north to south is an unsatisfactory 0.22% of the gnp of the rich countries. there is a link between this and what we are discussing here and this also defines the challenge we have to face.

commission. – the european commission is concerned by the political climate in togo. though mr messan, a local journalist, and mr olympio, leader of an opposition party, have recently been released, mr agboyibo remains in prison. recent reports suggest that more journalists have been arrested. the european union has several times conveyed its concern about the political climate to the government of togo. it made representations to the ministry of foreign affairs on 17 august. on that occasion, the union emphasised its desire that political parties and the media be able to operate freely. on 18 october, the union issued a declaration reiterating its concerns, emphasising the importance it attaches to the freedom, openness and transparency of the electoral process and calling on president eyadema to have mr agboyibo released. the commission has taken note of the government's decision to schedule parliamentary elections for 10 and 24 march next year. the commission has earmarked about eur 1.56 million to help prepare the elections. the funding will pay for electoral equipment and the printing of ballot papers. the financing agreement has been signed, the first contracts concluded counsel. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, politics often involves having several strings attached to one's bow so that one can adapt, when necessary, to ever-changing circumstances. indeed, six months ago our ambitious plans for the belgian presidency were openly criticized. more gently, we were advised to limit the goals to ensure that they were achieved and to ensure that everyone would talk about success. the attacks of september 11th upset our plans and changed the order of priorities of our ambitions to such an extent that we had to revise our agenda. fortunately, we had other ropes on our bow to prevent this change from turning into immobility. in conclusion, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i think we have achieved a great deal. let's start with a realization that, fortunately, is hardly talked about anymore. in less than three months, we have held three meetings at the highest level in belgium. the first was in brussels on 21 september, with an extraordinary council. in ghent, on 19 october, with an informal council. and then laeken, last friday and saturday. i think i can say that despite the large demonstrations, seven in all, and large, 80,000 people in brussels last thursday, the incidents were extremely limited - a few stalls destroyed, a rare case of hooliganism. that is why i would like to take this opportunity, if i may, to thank the police forces who have worked perfectly in ghent, brussels and other cities. they have, i believe, demonstrated the method to be followed: a discreet, unprovoked presence, a broad tolerance, which is normal in a democratic and open society, and a swift and severe intervention when a certain threshold is crossed. on the other hand, we took the other anti-globalists seriously. we talked to them. they actually taught us a lot. so i believe and hope that the blacklist of confrontations - seattle, nice, gothenburg, genoa - is now closed. i would naturally like to speak to you about the content, the substance of the laeken summit. what struck me yesterday, madam president, when i read the conclusions of this summit, was that i think we have achieved quite a lot in these two days of work. i know that public opinion always looks at such a summit with a thirst for spectacle, but such a meeting is essentially a way of moving things forward, of moving europe forward. the first step, and i think the most important, is the laeken declaration. in recent months, the text has been elaborated, reworked and refined, but the essential elements have not been changed. this statement must take account of the growing sense of alienation among the european citizen. it must above all be a completely different, i would say innovative, approach to the renewal of europe. that is why, as you know, we have created the convention. the convention will start on 1 march 2002. the national parliaments and the european parliament will be given an important role in this process, on an equal footing with the representatives of the heads of state and government, and in addition to these actors, there is a place for the candidate countries, the economic and social committee, the social partners, the regions and, in particular, the regions with legislative powers.

- madam president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr president of the commission, i have already had the opportunity to say that in my view the obsession of every european politician should be, in the coming period, to bridge the gap of distrust, if not of mistrust, which is constantly widening between the citizens and the european institutions. so anything that can help to open up the debate on the future of europe in our respective societies is, for my group, welcome. we therefore welcome the principle of the convention, which breaks with the conventional intergovernmental back door, involves european and national parliamentarians in the preparatory work for the igc, accepts the participation of representatives of the candidate countries and is open to the contributions of the social partners. be assured that we will encourage our civil society partners to invest constructively and without taboos in this new european political space. hopefully those who try to avoid addressing the troubling issues arising in our societies will not be followed by the majority of the convention. breaking the thermometer doesn't bring down the fever. i therefore found it stimulating, because it is in line with the reality experienced by our fellow citizens, the situation described in the draft declaration submitted by mr verhofstadt to the european council, but which the fifteen have unfortunately decided not to take up. i regret, however, that the presidency has not shown the same critical spirit in formulating the questions for discussion. the european council naturally found nothing wrong with that. the two vice-presidents of my group, mrs kaufmann and mrs frahm, will be looking at the institutional aspects of the laeken summit. i would like to emphasize one point in this connection. if, as the declaration of the fifteen says, it is really a question of using the expectations of the citizens as the guiding principle for the reflection that is to begin, then the debate cannot, in my view, dissociate the institutional questions of the european project from the political guidelines which these institutions are supposed to implement. anyone who has participated in citizen debates in the context of the pre-laeken consultation, or has taken the trouble to listen to the messages emanating from the major mobilizations of the last few days in brussels, has in mind the pressing demands that are practically absent from the agenda of the convention as defined by the laeken declaration. for example, the whole social question in the broadest sense of the word should give rise to debates about the new role to be played by the euro and the european central bank. it should lead to a more in-depth discussion of ideas on european services of general economic interest. it should lead to a re-examination of the dogma of the rationing of public expenditure, to a renewed reflection on the taxation of capital movements, and to a greater desire to put an end to fiscal dumping and tax havens. the union's economic policy should no longer be limited to competition policy, nor should its monetary policy be aligned solely on the requirements of financial markets. the question of the effective rights of employees in the face of the power of large groups, as well as the question of the effective involvement of citizens in the elaboration of european policies and the evaluation of their effects, are also, in my view, an essential theme from this point of view. all these questions in the minds of the people have an institutional dimension. they therefore have their place in the discussions of the future convention. the same applies to enlargement. is the institutional challenge posed by this historical perspective separable from the other crucial problems which we must urgently prevent? two figures are enough to assess the challenges we are not addressing, when we should be facing them with clarity and responsibility. in 2004, the union will have 30% more citizens, but its gdp will only increase by 4.5%. what structural reforms, and in particular what policy of solidarity, will be necessary to avoid dangerous tensions and to succeed in building what the laeken declaration calls a great european family? finally, the few lines devoted to the cfsp in this framework document are almost exclusively, and i quote, 'the re-actualisation of the petersberg tasks'. as if europe's ability to wage war was the guarantee of its international authority. i can testify, having had the opportunity in recent weeks to travel to several parts of the world, that this is not the first time we have been questioned. what is expected of europe is that it should help them to free themselves from the stifling tutelage of american hyperpower, that it should make the rule of unilateralism retreat in a much more offensive way, that it should develop a great strategy for conflict prevention by responding to the needs of the peoples of the south for development, equality and dignity, in short that it should bring to life a very different interpretation of the post-9/11 world than that of george w. bush. dare to open its windows on real life. let us give europe a clear and mobilizing meaning again, and i think that the institutional dynamic will be freed from this. at least that's what i think.
mr president, the debate on the future of europe is for some people reduced to the development of the community method: monopoly of initiative for the commission, political power and interpretation for the court of justice, the right to impose european law on one or more states by increasing majority decisions. this centralised vision of europe in ever more areas runs counter to the will of citizens who want to benefit from their differences. the irish, the only people to be consulted by referendum, were right to reject the treaty of nice. the convention will be a mere artifice if it pursues the same objective without starting from the fact that the treaty of nice is dead. unfortunately, the goals seem unchanging. the laeken conclusions welcome the progress made and the agreements reached on the liberalization of postal services, which will lead to a weakening of the social and territorial cohesion of our states. it is unacceptable to impose on all the choice of certain states to privatise and open up their public services to competition. it is not a proposal to bring the citizens of europe closer together, nor is it a condition for peace on the continent. the opposite approach is needed, namely to bring europe closer to the citizens. this requires listening to them and, once the genuinely shared concerns have been expressed, discussing a possible common response.
- mr president, in defining the agenda for the future convention on the future of the union, the laeken council departed from the conclusions of the nice council on two points of concern to us. firstly, whereas the nice declaration no 23 had included on the agenda an item entitled 'the role of national parliaments in the european architecture', the laeken council drowned this idea under a much more vague title, i quote: 'more democracy, transparency and efficiency in the european union'. under this heading, it asks first how to increase the democratic legitimacy of the current institutions and, secondly, whether the role of national parliaments should be changed. this is a very biased approach, because in reality the two issues are one and the same: recognising the prominent role of national parliaments within the european architecture is the best way of reconciling the union with its citizens. second amendment: while nice only referred in a neutral way to the status of the charter of fundamental rights, laeken put another idea on the agenda, the idea of a european constitution, that is to say, a fundamental text clearly supranational as opposed to a treaty. it is therefore clear, mr president, that between nice and laeken the federalist pressure groups have taken over again. they have succeeded in getting amendments through which, both of them very significant, tend to undermine the place of national democracies. this is not the direction our citizens want and will have to be corrected in the years to come.

- mr president, mr council representative, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european council meeting in laeken, which concluded the belgian presidency of the union, was a success. i say this not out of politeness or convenience but because i have the strong feeling that the heads of state and government have in recent days sent the signal that europeans were waiting for, that of clarity and rejection of falsehoods. the laeken summit achieved its main ambition: to adopt a declaration on the future of europe, paving the way for the future major reform of the union. as the president-in-office of the council has said, there were no taboos in laeken, no questions were avoided, and i hope that this formula will become a reality, because the construction of europe has too often been opaque, or at least reserved for the insiders. i should like to ask you, on behalf of the french delegation of the epp-ed group, to welcome the appointment of mr valéry giscard d'estaing as president of the convention and of mr giuliano amato and mr jean-luc dehaene as vice-presidents. these eminent personalities are recognised for their experience and for their determination to bring about a change in attitudes in favour of a europe which fully and democratically assumes its competences, but only its clearly defined competences. at a time when europe is acquiring a currency, is expanding, is trying to give a soul and values to globalisation, it is high time to reconsider our conception of public life and the relationship between citizens and their institutions at all levels. a milestone has been reached in laeken. we look forward to it. but there's still a long way to go. so let us not give up.
- mr president, in the aftermath of the laeken summit, i would like to express some regrets and some hope. i regret that the heads of state or government meeting in laeken have not been able to demonstrate their capacity to act on foreign and defence policy. so, at a time of unprecedented crisis, the european union has not been able to decide whether to send a joint force to afghanistan. this decision would have given a strong signal of the will of the europeans, showing that we were ready to assume our responsibilities fully, both militarily and humanitarian or political. similarly, once again, no immediate decision was taken on the matter of common defence. the announcements remained largely virtual and the question of automatic eu access to nato assets was not resolved. the union's foreign and defence policy is more in words than in deeds, and i regret that. more than ever, we must build a political and democratic europe which can have a weight and influence in the world. that is why i would now like to express a hope. the laeken summit decided to set up the convention. it has provided it with an excellent president and an open agenda. i would like to thank the belgian presidency, which has shown courage and vision throughout its term of office, and the commissioner responsible for these matters. this convention opens the way to a new future for europe. i hope that it will succeed, that in two years' time we will have a constitution that is readable and understandable by all the citizens of the european union, and that we will finally put an end to the principle of direct election of the president of the european commission. if we do not want the european union to be just a free trade area tomorrow, if we really want to have a say in the world, in the new international order, this is the only way.
